translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 77
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 77

sentences.zh: 【魏紀九】起柔兆困敦，盡重光大荒落，凡六年。

translations.literal: [Wei Records 9] From Rouzhao Kundun through Chongguang Dahuangluo, six years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Records of Wei, Number Nine] Spanning from the cyclical year Rouzhao Kundun through Chongguang Dahuangluo—six years in all.

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公下甘露元年（

translations.literal: Under the Duke of Gaoguixiang, first year of Ganlu (
translations.idiomatic: Under the Duke of Gaoguixiang, first year of Ganlu (

sentences.zh: 丙子，公元二五六年）

translations.literal: bingzi, AD 256)
translations.idiomatic: the year bingzi, AD 256)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，漢姜維進位大將軍。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, Han's Jiang Wei was promoted to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Jiang Wei of Shu was promoted to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙辰，帝宴群臣於太極東堂，與諸儒論夏少康、漢高祖優劣，以少康為優。

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingchen, the Emperor entertained the ministers at the eastern hall of the Taiji Palace, debating with the scholars the relative merits of Xia's Shaokang and Han's Gaozu, deeming Shaokang superior.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day bingchen, the emperor feasted his ministers in the eastern hall of the Hall of Supreme Harmony and debated with the classical scholars whether Xia's Shaokang or Han's founding emperor was the greater ruler, ruling in favor of Shaokang.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚戌，賜大將軍昭袞冕之服，赤舄副焉。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on gengxu, the Grand General Zhao was granted the robes of the nine-symbol regalia and red shoes as accessories.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on the day gengxu, Grand General Sima Zhao was granted the nine-symbol imperial regalia and matching red ceremonial shoes.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，帝幸太學，與諸儒論《書》、《易》及《禮》，諸儒莫能及。

translations.literal: On bingchen, the Emperor visited the Imperial Academy and debated the Book of Documents, the Book of Changes, and the Rites with the scholars; none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingchen, the emperor visited the Imperial Academy and discussed the Book of Documents, the Book of Changes, and the Rites with the scholars, and none could keep pace with him.

sentences.zh: 帝常與中護軍司馬望、侍中王沈、散騎常侍裴秀、黃門侍郎鐘會等講宴於東堂，並屬文論，特加禮異，謂秀為儒林丈人，沈為文籍先生。

translations.literal: The Emperor often lectured and feasted at the eastern hall with Central Protector of the Army Sima Wang, Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Shen, Cavalier Attendant Pei Xiu, Yellow Gate Attendant Zhong Hui, and others, composing essays and discoursing together; he showed them special honor, calling Xiu the Elder of the Confucian Grove and Shen the Master of Literary Records.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often held literary discussions and banquets in the eastern hall with Central Protector of the Army Sima Wang, Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Shen, Cavalier Attendant Pei Xiu, Yellow Gate Attendant Zhong Hui, and others; he treated them with exceptional courtesy, styling Xiu the Elder of the Confucian Grove and Shen the Master of Literary Records.

sentences.zh: 帝性急，請召欲速，以望職在外，特給追鋒車、虎賁五人，每有集會，輒奔馳而至。

translations.literal: The Emperor was impatient by nature and wished summonses to be swift; because Wang's post kept him outside the palace, he was specially given a courier's chariot and five tiger guards, and whenever there was a gathering he would gallop to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impatient by nature and wanted his summons answered at once; because Wang's duties kept him outside the palace, he was given a courier's chariot and five tiger guards so that whenever the court assembled he could ride at full speed to attend.

sentences.zh: 秀，潛之子也。

translations.literal: Xiu was the son of Pei Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xiu was the son of Pei Qian.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙午，改元。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingwu, the reign era was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day bingwu, the reign era was changed.

sentences.zh: 姜維在鐘提，議者多以為維力已竭，未能更出。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei was at Zhongti; most of those who deliberated held that Wei's strength was already exhausted and that he could not campaign again.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei was encamped at Zhongti, and most at court believed his strength was spent and that he would not mount another campaign.

sentences.zh: 安西將軍鄧艾曰：「洮西之敗，非小失也，士卒彫殘，倉廩空虛，百姓流離。

translations.literal: Anxi General Deng Ai said: "The defeat west of the Tao was no minor setback—the troops are worn down, the granaries empty, and the people displaced.
translations.idiomatic: Anxi General Deng Ai said, "The defeat west of the Tao was no minor setback. Our troops are worn down, the granaries empty, and the people displaced.

sentences.zh: 今以策言之，彼有乘勝之勢，我有虛弱之實，一也。

translations.literal: Judging by strategy now, they have the momentum of victory while we have the reality of weakness—that is the first point.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by strategy, they have the momentum of victory while we are genuinely weak—that is the first point.

sentences.zh: 彼上下相習，五兵犀利，我將易兵新，器仗未復，二也。

translations.literal: Their officers and men are accustomed to one another and their five weapons are sharp; our generals are newly changed, our troops are new, and our arms are not yet restored—that is the second point.
translations.idiomatic: Their commanders and troops work in concert and their weapons are keen; we have new generals, green troops, and arms not yet replenished—that is the second point.

sentences.zh: 彼以船行，吾以陸軍，勞逸不同，三也。

translations.literal: They travel by boat while we march by land—the difference in toil and rest is the third point.
translations.idiomatic: They move by water while we march overland—the difference in fatigue is the third point.

sentences.zh: 狄道、隴西、南安、祁山各當有守，彼專為一，我分為四，四也。

translations.literal: Didao, Longxi, Nan'an, and Qishan each require garrisons; they concentrate on one objective while we are divided into four—that is the fourth point.
translations.idiomatic: Didao, Longxi, Nan'an, and Qishan each need defenders; they can focus on one target while we are split four ways—that is the fourth point.

sentences.zh: 從南安、隴西因食羌谷，若趣祁山，熟麥千頃，為之外倉，五也。

translations.literal: Passing through Nan'an and Longxi they can live off Qiang grain; if they press toward Qishan, a thousand qing of ripe wheat will serve as their external granary—that is the fifth point.
translations.idiomatic: Marching through Nan'an and Longxi they can live off Qiang grain, and if they drive on Qishan a thousand qing of ripe wheat will serve as their forward supply—that is the fifth point.

sentences.zh: 賊有黠計，其來必矣。

translations.literal: The enemy has cunning schemes—they are certain to come.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is cunning; they are certain to come.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，姜維復率眾出祁山，聞鄧艾已有備，乃回，從董亭趣南安；

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, Jiang Wei again led his forces out toward Qishan; hearing that Deng Ai was already prepared, he turned back and marched from Dongting toward Nan'an;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Jiang Wei again led his army toward Qishan. Learning that Deng Ai was already prepared, he withdrew and marched from Dongting toward Nan'an;

sentences.zh: 艾據武城山以拒之。

translations.literal: Ai occupied Wucheng Mountain to block him.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai seized Wucheng Mountain to block his advance.

sentences.zh: 維與艾爭險不克，其夜，渡渭東行，緣山趣上邽。

translations.literal: Wei and Ai contested the passes without success; that night he crossed the Wei eastward and followed the mountains toward Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Ai fought for the passes without success. That night he crossed the Wei to the east and followed the mountain routes toward Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 艾與戰於段谷，大破之。

translations.literal: Ai engaged him at Duangu and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai met him at Duangu and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 以艾為鎮西將軍，都督隴右諸軍事。

translations.literal: Ai was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and put in overall command of military affairs in Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and given overall command of military affairs in Longyou.

sentences.zh: 維與其鎮西大將軍胡濟期會上邽，濟失期，不至，故敗，士卒星散，死者甚眾，蜀人由是怨維。

translations.literal: Wei had arranged to meet his General Who Pacifies the West Hu Ji at Shanggui; Ji missed the rendezvous and did not arrive, and therefore they were defeated—the troops scattered like stars, and the dead were very many; the people of Shu henceforth resented Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had arranged to rendezvous at Shanggui with General Who Pacifies the West Hu Ji, but Ji failed to appear on time, and so they were defeated. The troops scattered in every direction and casualties were heavy; from this the people of Shu turned against Jiang Wei.

sentences.zh: 維上書謝，求自貶黜；

translations.literal: Wei submitted a memorial apologizing and asking to demote himself;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei submitted a memorial of apology and asked to be reduced in rank;

sentences.zh: 乃以衛將軍行大將軍事。

translations.literal: he was therefore made Defender General acting in the capacity of Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: he was therefore made Defender General with authority to act as Grand General.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚午，詔司馬昭加號大都督，奏事不名，假黃鉞。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on gengwu, an edict added to Sima Zhao the title Grand Commander, exempted him from having his name tabooed in memorials, and lent him the yellow battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day gengwu, an edict gave Sima Zhao the additional title Grand Commander, exempted his name from taboo in memorials to the throne, and lent him the yellow battle-axe.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以太尉司馬孚為太傅。

translations.literal: On guiyou, the Grand Commandant Sima Fu was made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guiyou, Grand Commandant Sima Fu was appointed Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 九月，以司徒高柔為太尉。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Minister of Works Gao Rou was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Minister of Works Gao Rou was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 文欽說吳人以伐魏之利，孫峻使欽與驃騎將軍呂擾及車騎將軍劉纂、鎮南將軍朱異、前將軍唐咨自江都入淮、泗，以圖青、徐。

translations.literal: Wen Qin persuaded the Wu people of the advantages of attacking Wei; Sun Jun sent Qin with Rapid-as-Lightning General Lü Rao, Chariots-and-Cavalry General Liu Zuan, General Who Pacifies the South Zhu Yi, and Forward General Tang Zi from Jiangdu into the Huai and Si rivers to target Qing and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin persuaded Wu of the advantages of striking Wei. Sun Jun sent Qin with Rapid-as-Lightning General Lü Rao, Chariots-and-Cavalry General Liu Zuan, General Who Pacifies the South Zhu Yi, and Forward General Tang Zi from Jiangdu into the Huai and Si to target Qing and Xu provinces.

sentences.zh: 峻餞之於石頭，遇暴疾，以後事付從父弟偏將軍綝。

translations.literal: Jun gave them a farewell feast at Shitou, then suffered a sudden illness and entrusted subsequent affairs to his father's younger brother's son, Partial General Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Jun gave them a farewell feast at Shitou, then fell suddenly ill and entrusted affairs to his cousin, Partial General Sun Lin.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，峻卒。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Jun died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dinghai, Sun Jun died.

sentences.zh: 吳人以綝為侍中、武衛將軍、都督中外諸軍事，召呂據等還。

translations.literal: The Wu court made Lin Attendant-in-Ordinary, Martial Guard General, and commander of all military affairs inside and outside the court, and recalled Lü Ju and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Wu appointed Lin Attendant-in-Ordinary, Martial Guard General, and overall commander of military affairs, and recalled Lü Ju and the others.

sentences.zh: 己丑，吳大司馬呂岱卒，年九十六。

translations.literal: On jichou, Wu's Grand Marshal Lü Dai died at the age of ninety-six.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jichou, Wu's Grand Marshal Lü Dai died at the age of ninety-six.

sentences.zh: 始岱親近吳郡徐原，慷慨有才志，岱知其可成，賜巾韝，與共言論，後遂薦拔，官至侍御史。

translations.literal: Earlier Dai had been close to Xu Yuan of Wu commandery, a man of generous spirit and talent; Dai knew he could succeed, gave him a headcloth and armguard, and discussed matters with him; he later recommended and promoted him, and Yuan rose to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Dai had taken a liking to Xu Yuan of Wu commandery, a man of generous spirit and real ability. Dai saw his promise, gave him a scholar's cap and armguard, and talked matters over with him; he later recommended him for office, and Yuan rose to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 原性忠壯，好直言。

translations.literal: Yuan's nature was loyal and forthright; he loved to speak plainly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was loyal and forthright and loved to speak his mind plainly.

sentences.zh: 岱時有得失，原輒諫爭，又公論之。

translations.literal: Whenever Dai had successes or failures, Yuan would remonstrate and dispute, and also discuss them publicly.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Dai erred or succeeded, Yuan would remonstrate with him and also air the matter in public discussion.

sentences.zh: 人或以告岱，岱歎曰：「是我所以貴德淵者也！

translations.literal: Some told Dai of this; Dai sighed and said: "This is why I esteem Deyuan!
translations.idiomatic: When someone reported this to Dai, he sighed and said, "That is why I value Deyuan!

sentences.zh: 」及原死，岱哭之甚哀，曰：「徐德淵，呂岱之益友，今不幸，岱復於何聞過！

translations.literal: " When Yuan died, Dai wept for him most bitterly and said: "Xu Deyuan was Lü Dai's beneficial friend; now that misfortune has befallen him, from whom shall Dai hear of his faults!
translations.idiomatic: " When Yuan died, Dai mourned him deeply and said, "Xu Deyuan was Lü Dai's true friend. Now that he is gone, from whom shall I hear of my faults?

sentences.zh: 」談者美之。

translations.literal: " Those who discussed the matter praised him.
translations.idiomatic: " Commentators praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 呂據聞孫綝代孫峻輔政，大怒，與諸督將連名共表薦滕胤為丞相；

translations.literal: Lü Ju, hearing that Sun Lin had replaced Sun Jun in assisting the government, was greatly angered and, with the various supervising generals signing jointly, submitted a memorial recommending Teng Yin as Chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Ju learned that Sun Lin had replaced Sun Jun as regent, he was furious. He and the frontier generals submitted a joint memorial recommending Teng Yin as chancellor;

sentences.zh: 綝更以胤為大司馬，代呂岱駐武昌。

translations.literal: Lin instead made Yin Grand Marshal, replacing Lü Dai in garrisoning Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Lin instead appointed Yin Grand Marshal and sent him to replace Lü Dai at the garrison in Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 據引兵還，使人報胤，欲共廢綝。

translations.literal: Ju led his troops back and sent word to Yin, wishing to depose Lin together.
translations.idiomatic: Ju marched his troops back and sent word to Yin that they should depose Lin together.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁未，綝遣從兄憲將兵逆據於江都，使中使敕文欽、劉纂、唐咨等共擊取據，又遣侍中左將軍華融、中書丞丁晏告喻胤宜速去意。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on dingwei, Lin sent his elder cousin's son Xian with troops to oppose Ju at Jiangdu, ordered palace envoys to command Wen Qin, Liu Zuan, Tang Zi, and the rest to join in attacking Ju, and also sent Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left General Hua Rong and Secretariat Assistant Ding Yan to inform Yin that he should withdraw promptly.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day dingwei, Lin sent his cousin Sun Xian with troops to block Ju at Jiangdu, ordered palace envoys to direct Wen Qin, Liu Zuan, Tang Zi, and the others to join the attack on Ju, and sent Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left General Hua Rong and Secretariat Assistant Ding Yan to warn Yin to withdraw at once.

sentences.zh: 胤自以禍及，因留融、晏、勒兵自衛，召典軍楊崇、將軍孫咨，告以綝為亂，迫融等使作書難綝。

translations.literal: Yin, believing disaster was upon him, detained Rong and Yan, mustered troops to defend himself, summoned Director of the Army Yang Chong and General Sun Zi, told them that Lin was in rebellion, and compelled Rong and the others to draft a letter denouncing Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, seeing disaster closing in, detained Rong and Yan, mustered troops for his own defense, summoned Director of the Army Yang Chong and General Sun Zi, told them Lin was rebelling, and forced Rong and the others to draft a denunciation of Lin.

sentences.zh: 綝不聽，表言胤反，許將軍劉丞以封爵，使率兵騎攻圍胤。

translations.literal: Lin would not listen; he memorialized that Yin had rebelled, promised General Liu Cheng a fief and noble rank, and sent him leading cavalry and infantry to attack and besiege Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Lin paid no heed. He reported that Yin had rebelled, promised General Liu Cheng a fief and noble title, and sent him with cavalry and infantry to besiege Yin.

sentences.zh: 胤又劫融等使詐為詔發兵，融等不從，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Yin again coerced Rong and the others to forge an edict to raise troops; they would not comply and he killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Yin then tried to force Rong and the others to forge an edict mobilizing troops; when they refused, he killed them all.

sentences.zh: 或勸胤引兵至蒼龍門：「將士見公出，必委絲林就公。

translations.literal: Some urged Yin to lead his troops to the Azure Dragon Gate: "When the officers and men see you emerge, they will abandon Silin and rally to you.
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Yin to march to the Azure Dragon Gate, saying, "When the troops see you come out, they will abandon Sun Lin and join you.

sentences.zh: 」時夜已半，胤恃與據期，又難舉兵向宮，乃約令部曲，說呂侯兵已在近道，故皆為胤盡死，無離散者。

translations.literal: " It was already midnight; Yin relied on his rendezvous with Ju and also found it hard to march against the palace, so he merely bound his subordinates with pledges, saying Marquis Lü's troops were already on the near road—therefore all died for Yin to the last man, with none deserting.
translations.idiomatic: " It was already midnight. Yin was counting on Ju's arrival and hesitated to march on the palace, so he only bound his followers with pledges, claiming Lü Ju's army was close at hand. They all fought to the death for him, and none deserted.

sentences.zh: 胤顏色不變，談笑如常。

translations.literal: Yin's expression did not change; he talked and laughed as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's expression never changed; he talked and laughed as usual.

sentences.zh: 時大風，比曉，據不至，綝兵大會，遂殺胤及將士數十人，夷胤三族。

translations.literal: A great wind was blowing; by dawn Ju had not arrived and Lin's troops had massed, so they killed Yin and several tens of officers and men and exterminated Yin's clan to the third degree.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce wind was blowing. By dawn Ju had still not come, while Lin's forces had gathered in strength. They killed Yin and several dozen of his officers and men and exterminated his clan to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 己酉，大赦，改元太平。

translations.literal: On jiyou, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiyou, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Taiping.

sentences.zh: 或勸呂據奔魏者，據曰：「吾恥為叛臣。

translations.literal: Some urged Lü Ju to flee to Wei; Ju said: "I would be ashamed to become a rebel minister.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Lü Ju to flee to Wei. Ju said, "I would be ashamed to become a turncoat.

sentences.zh: 」遂自殺。

translations.literal: " He then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: " He then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 以司空鄭沖為司徒，左僕射盧毓為司空。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works Zheng Chong was made Minister over the Masses, and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Lu Yu was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zheng Chong was appointed Minister over the Masses, and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Lu Yu was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 毓固讓驃騎將軍王昶、光祿大夫王觀、司隸校尉琅邪王祥，詔不許。

translations.literal: Yu firmly declined in favor of Rapid-as-Lightning General Wang Chang, Household Counsellor Wang Guan, and Director of the Secretariat Wang Xiang of Langye; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu firmly offered the post to Rapid-as-Lightning General Wang Chang, Household Counsellor Wang Guan, and Director of the Secretariat Wang Xiang of Langye, but the edict refused.

sentences.zh: 祥性至孝，繼母朱氏遇之無道，祥愈恭謹。

translations.literal: Xiang's nature was supremely filial; his stepmother the Zhu clan treated him without decency, yet Xiang became all the more respectful and careful.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was profoundly filial. His stepmother, Lady Zhu, treated him harshly, yet he became only more respectful and careful.

sentences.zh: 朱氏子覽，年數歲，每見祥被楚撻，輒涕泣抱持母；

translations.literal: The Zhu clan's son Lan was several years old; whenever he saw Xiang beaten with the rod he would weep and cling to his mother;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhu's son Lan was still a small boy. Whenever he saw Xiang beaten with the rod, he would weep and cling to his mother;

sentences.zh: 母以非理使祥，覽輒與祥俱往。

translations.literal: when the mother sent Xiang on some unreasonable errand, Lan would go together with Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: and when his mother sent Xiang on some unreasonable errand, Lan would go along with him.

sentences.zh: 及長，娶妻，母虐使祥妻，覽妻亦趨而共之。

translations.literal: When he grew up and took a wife, the mother cruelly worked Xiang's wife, and Lan's wife would hurry to share the labor.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up and married, his mother mistreated Xiang's wife, and Lan's wife would hurry to share the work with her.

sentences.zh: 母患之，為之少止。

translations.literal: The mother resented this and for his sake eased off somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The mother resented this and eased off somewhat on their account.

sentences.zh: 祥漸有時譽，母深疾之，密使鴆祥。

translations.literal: Xiang gradually gained a reputation in his time; the mother deeply hated this and secretly had him poisoned.
translations.idiomatic: As Xiang gradually won a public reputation, his mother came to hate him deeply and secretly arranged to poison him.

sentences.zh: 覽知之，逕起取酒，祥爭而不與，母遽奪反之。

translations.literal: Lan learned of it, rose straightway and took the wine; Xiang struggled and would not give it, and the mother hastily snatched it back.
translations.idiomatic: Lan learned of it, rose at once, and took the wine. Xiang struggled to keep it from him, and their mother snatched it back in alarm.

sentences.zh: 自後，母賜祥饌，覽輒先嘗。

translations.literal: After that, whenever the mother gave Xiang food, Lan would taste it first.
translations.idiomatic: After that, whenever his mother sent food to Xiang, Lan would taste it first.

sentences.zh: 母懼覽致斃，遂止。

translations.literal: The mother feared Lan would die and therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Lan might die, she stopped.

sentences.zh: 漢末遭亂，祥隱居三十餘年，不應州郡之命，母終，毀瘁，杖而後起。

translations.literal: At the end of Han he encountered turmoil; Xiang lived in seclusion for more than thirty years and did not respond to summons from the provinces and commanderies; when his mother died he was wasted with grief and could rise only with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Han, amid the turmoil, Xiang lived in seclusion for more than thirty years and ignored summons from the provinces and commanderies. When his mother died he was wasted with grief and could rise only with a staff.

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史呂虔檄為別駕，委以州事，州界清靜，政化大行。

translations.literal: Xuzhou Inspector Lü Qian summoned him by official letter as Chief Assistant and entrusted him with the affairs of the province; the borders of the province were tranquil and good government flourished widely.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou Inspector Lü Qian summoned him as Chief Assistant and entrusted him with provincial affairs. The region grew peaceful and his reforms took hold throughout the province.

sentences.zh: 時人歌之曰：「海沂之康，實賴王祥；

translations.literal: People of the time sang of him, saying: "The peace of the sea-shore and Yi River region truly depends on Wang Xiang;
translations.idiomatic: People of the time sang of him, saying, "The peace of the coast and Yi country truly rests on Wang Xiang;

sentences.zh: 邦國不空，別駕之功！

translations.literal: the state is not left vacant—the Chief Assistant's achievement!
translations.idiomatic: the realm is not left empty—it is the Chief Assistant's doing!"

sentences.zh: 十一月，吳孫綝遷大將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Wu's Sun Lin was transferred to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Sun Lin of Wu was promoted to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 綝負貴倨傲，多行無禮。

translations.literal: Lin relied on his exalted rank and was arrogant, often acting without propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Lin traded on his exalted rank, was arrogant, and often behaved without propriety.

sentences.zh: 峻從弟憲嘗與誅諸葛恪，峻厚遇之，官至右將軍、無難督，平九官事。

translations.literal: Jun's younger cousin's son Xian had once joined in executing Zhuge Ke; Jun treated him generously, and he rose to Right General, Supervisor of Wunan, and oversaw the affairs of the Nine Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's cousin Sun Xian had taken part in the execution of Zhuge Ke. Jun treated him generously, and he rose to Right General, Supervisor of Wunan, with authority over the Nine Offices.

sentences.zh: 綝遇憲薄於峻時，憲怒，與將軍王惇謀殺綝。

translations.literal: Lin treated Xian more poorly than Jun had; Xian was angry and plotted with General Wang Dun to kill Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Lin treated Xian less well than Jun had, and Xian, enraged, plotted with General Wang Dun to kill Lin.

sentences.zh: 事洩，綝殺惇，憲服藥死。

translations.literal: The affair leaked out; Lin killed Dun, and Xian took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered. Lin killed Dun, and Xian took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公下甘露二年（

translations.literal: Under the Duke of Gaoguixiang, second year of Ganlu (
translations.idiomatic: Under the Duke of Gaoguixiang, second year of Ganlu (

sentences.zh: 丁丑，公元二五七年）

translations.literal: dingchou, AD 257)
translations.idiomatic: the year dingchou, AD 257)

sentences.zh: 春，三月，大梁成侯盧毓卒。

translations.literal: In spring, in the third month, Marquis Cheng of Daliang, Lu Yu, died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the third month, Marquis Cheng of Daliang, Lu Yu, died.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，吳主臨正殿，大赦，始親政事。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, the Wu ruler attended the main hall, proclaimed a general amnesty, and for the first time personally handled government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, the Wu ruler took his seat in the main hall, proclaimed a general amnesty, and for the first time personally attended to government affairs.

sentences.zh: 孫綝表奏，多見難問，又科兵子弟十八已下，十五以上三千餘人，選大將子弟年少有勇力者，使將之，日於苑中教習，曰：「吾立此軍，欲與之俱長。

translations.literal: Sun Lin's memorials were often met with difficult questioning; he also mustered more than three thousand sons of military families aged fifteen and above but under eighteen, chose young men of courage and strength among the sons of great generals to command them, and had them drilled daily in the park, saying: "I am establishing this army to grow up together with it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin's memorials were often sharply questioned. He also conscripted more than three thousand sons of military families between fifteen and eighteen, chose the young and brave among the sons of great generals to lead them, and had them drilled daily in the imperial park, saying, "I am raising this army to grow up together with it.

sentences.zh: 」又數出中書視大帝時舊事，問左右侍臣曰：「先帝數有特製，今大將軍問事，但令我書可邪？

translations.literal: " He also repeatedly went to the Secretariat to review old matters from the time of the Great Emperor and asked the attendants at his side: "The late emperor often had special regulations; now when the Grand General inquires into affairs, am I only to write my approval?
translations.idiomatic: " He also went repeatedly to the Secretariat to review records from the reign of the founding emperor and asked his attendants, "The late emperor often issued special orders. Now when the Grand General inquires into affairs, am I only to write my approval?

sentences.zh: 」嘗食生梅，使黃門至中藏取蜜，蜜中有鼠矢；

translations.literal: " Once, eating raw plums, he sent a Yellow Gate attendant to the central storehouse for honey; there was rat droppings in the honey;
translations.idiomatic: " Once, while eating raw plums, he sent a Yellow Gate attendant to the central storehouse for honey and found rat droppings in it;

sentences.zh: 召問藏吏，藏吏叩頭。

translations.literal: he summoned and questioned the storehouse clerk, who kowtowed.
translations.idiomatic: he summoned the storehouse clerk, who prostrated himself at once.

sentences.zh: 吳主曰：「黃門從爾求蜜邪？

translations.literal: The Wu ruler said: "Did the Yellow Gate attendant ask honey from you?
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler said, "Did the Yellow Gate attendant ask you for honey?

sentences.zh: 」吏曰：「向求，實不敢與。

translations.literal: " The clerk said: "He did ask earlier, but I truly dared not give it.
translations.idiomatic: " The clerk said, "He did ask earlier, but I truly dared not give it to him.

sentences.zh: 」黃門不服。

translations.literal: " The Yellow Gate attendant would not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Yellow Gate attendant denied it.

sentences.zh: 吳主令破鼠矢，矢中燥，因大笑，謂左右曰：「若矢先在蜜中，中外當俱濕；

translations.literal: The Wu ruler ordered the rat droppings broken open; the inside was dry, and he therefore laughed loudly and said to those at his side: "If the droppings had been in the honey first, inside and outside should both be wet;
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler ordered the droppings broken open. The inside was dry, and he laughed and said to those around him, "If the droppings had been in the honey first, the inside and outside would both be wet;

sentences.zh: 今外濕裡燥，此必黃門所為也。

translations.literal: now the outside is wet and the inside dry—this must be the Yellow Gate attendant's doing.
translations.idiomatic: but the outside is wet and the inside dry. This must be the Yellow Gate attendant's doing.

sentences.zh: 」詰之，果服，左右莫不驚悚。

translations.literal: " He interrogated him and the man indeed confessed; those at his side were all startled.
translations.idiomatic: " He questioned him further, and the attendant confessed. Everyone present was astonished.

sentences.zh: 征東大將軍諸葛誕素與夏侯玄、鄧颺等友善，玄等死，王凌、毌丘儉相繼誅滅，誕內不自安，乃傾帑藏振施，曲赦有罪，以收眾心，畜養揚州輕俠數千人以為死士。

translations.literal: Eastern Campaign Grand General Zhuge Dan had always been on friendly terms with Xiahou Xuan, Deng Yang, and the like; when Xuan and the others died and Wang Ling and Guanqiu Jian were executed one after another, Dan was inwardly ill at ease; he therefore emptied the treasury to give relief, granted irregular pardons to the guilty to win popular hearts, and reared several thousand gallant adventurers of Yangzhou as death-loyal followers.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Campaign Grand General Zhuge Dan had long been friendly with Xiahou Xuan, Deng Yang, and their circle. After their deaths, and with Wang Ling and Guanqiu Jian executed in turn, Dan grew uneasy. He emptied the treasury for relief works, granted irregular pardons to win hearts, and kept several thousand Yangzhou bravoes as men willing to die for him.

sentences.zh: 因吳人欲向徐堨，請十萬眾以守壽春，又求臨淮築城以備吳寇。

translations.literal: Because the Wu people intended to move on Xuchui, he requested a hundred thousand troops to defend Shouchun and also asked to build a city at Linhuai to guard against Wu invaders.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu threatened Xuchui, he asked for a hundred thousand men to hold Shouchun and permission to build a fortress at Linhuai against Wu.

sentences.zh: 司馬昭初秉政，長史賈充請遣參佐慰勞四征，且觀其志。

translations.literal: When Sima Zhao first took power, Chief Clerk Jia Chong asked to send aides to console and comfort the four frontier generals and observe their intentions.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhao first took power, Chief Clerk Jia Chong proposed sending aides to console the four frontier generals and gauge their intentions.

sentences.zh: 昭遣充至淮南，充見誕，論說時事，因曰：「洛中諸賢，皆願禪代，君以為如何？

translations.literal: Zhao sent Chong to Huainan; Chong saw Dan and discussed current affairs, then said: "The worthies in Luoyang all wish to transfer the mandate—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: Zhao sent Chong to Huainan. Chong met Dan, discussed current affairs, and then said, "The worthies in Luoyang all favor transferring the mandate. What is your view?

sentences.zh: 」誕厲聲曰：「卿非賈豫州子乎？

translations.literal: " Dan said in a harsh voice: "Are you not the son of Jia of Yuzhou?
translations.idiomatic: " Dan said sharply, "Are you not the son of Jia of Yuzhou?

sentences.zh: 世受魏恩，豈可欲以社稷輸人乎！

translations.literal: Your family has received Wei's grace for generations—how can you wish to hand the altars of state over to others!
translations.idiomatic: Your family has received Wei's grace for generations. How can you wish to hand the realm over to others!

sentences.zh: 右洛中有難，吾當死之。

translations.literal: If trouble arises in Luoyang, I shall die for it.
translations.idiomatic: If trouble arises in Luoyang, I shall die defending the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 」充默然。

translations.literal: " Chong was silent.
translations.idiomatic: " Chong said nothing.

sentences.zh: 還，言於昭曰：「諸葛誕再在揚州，得士眾心。

translations.literal: On returning, he said to Zhao: "Zhuge Dan has again been in Yang Province and has won the hearts of officers and people.
translations.idiomatic: On returning, he reported to Sima Zhao, "Zhuge Dan's second tenure in Yang Province has won him the loyalty of officers and common soldiers alike.

sentences.zh: 今召之，必不來，然反疾而禍小；

translations.literal: If he is summoned now, he will surely not come, yet his rebellion will come quickly and the harm will be small;
translations.idiomatic: If you summon him now, he will surely refuse, but his rebellion will come quickly and the damage will be minor;

sentences.zh: 不召，則反遲而禍大；

translations.literal: if he is not summoned, then his rebellion will come late and the harm will be great;
translations.idiomatic: if you do not summon him, his rebellion will come later and the damage will be far greater;

sentences.zh: 不如召之。

translations.literal: it would be better to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: it would be better to summon him.

sentences.zh: 」昭從之。

translations.literal: " Zhao followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Zhao agreed.

sentences.zh: 甲子，詔以誕為司空，召赴京師。

translations.literal: On jia-zi, an edict appointed Dan Minister of Works and summoned him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jia-zi, an edict made Zhuge Dan Minister of Works and summoned him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 誕得詔書，愈恐，疑揚州刺史樂綝間己，遂殺綝，斂淮南及淮北郡縣屯田口十餘萬官兵，揚州新附勝兵者四五萬人，聚谷足一年食，為閉門自守之計。

translations.literal: When Dan received the edict, he grew ever more fearful; suspecting that Inspector of Yang Province Yue Lin was acting against him, he thereupon killed Lin. He gathered more than a hundred thousand officers and men from the military colonies of the commanderies and counties of Huainan and north of the Huai, together with forty or fifty thousand able-bodied troops newly attached to Yang Province, stored grain sufficient for one year's food, and planned to shut the gates and hold out on his own.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan received the edict, his fear deepened. Suspecting that Yue Lin, Inspector of Yang Province, was working against him, he killed Lin. He mustered more than a hundred thousand officers and men from the military colonies across Huainan and north of the Huai, added forty or fifty thousand able-bodied troops newly attached to Yang Province, stockpiled grain enough for a year, and prepared to shut the gates and defend himself.

sentences.zh: 遣長史吳綱將小子靚至吳，稱臣請救，並請以牙門子弟為質。

translations.literal: He sent Chief Clerk Wu Gang, leading his young son Jing, to Wu, declared himself a subject and asked for rescue, and also asked to leave the sons of his gate guards as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Chief Clerk Wu Gang with his young son Jing to Wu, submitted as a vassal and pleaded for aid, and offered the sons of his gate guards as hostages.

sentences.zh: 吳滕胤、呂據之妻，皆夏口督孫壹之妹也。

translations.literal: The wives of Wu's Teng Yin and Lü Ju were both younger sisters of Sun Yi, Supervisor of Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu, the wives of Teng Yin and Lü Ju were both younger sisters of Sun Yi, Supervisor of Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 六月，孫綝使鎮南將軍朱異自虎林將兵襲壹。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Sun Chen sent General Who Guards the South Zhu Yi from Hulin to lead troops in an attack on Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Sun Chen ordered General Who Guards the South Zhu Yi to lead troops from Hulin in an assault on Sun Yi.

sentences.zh: 異至武昌，壹將部曲來奔。

translations.literal: When Yi reached Wuchang, Yi led his personal forces to come and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Yi reached Wuchang, Sun Yi led his personal troops across to surrender.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，詔拜壹車騎將軍、交州牧，封吳侯，開府辟召，儀同三司，袞冕赤舄，事從豐厚。

translations.literal: On yi-si, an edict enfeoffed Yi as General of Chariots and Cavalry, Governor of Jiaozhou, and Marquis of Wu, with authorization to open an office and recruit staff, protocol equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, robe with twelve pendants and red shoes, and lavish provision in all matters.
translations.idiomatic: On yi-si, an edict made Sun Yi General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Jiaozhou, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wu, authorized him to open a personal office and recruit staff, granted him protocol equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, a twelve-pendant robe and red ceremonial shoes, and lavish provision in all matters.

sentences.zh: 司馬昭奉帝及太后討諸葛誕。

translations.literal: Sima Zhao, accompanying the Emperor and Empress Dowager, marched against Zhuge Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao accompanied the Emperor and Empress Dowager on campaign against Zhuge Dan.

sentences.zh: 吳綱至吳，吳人大喜，使將軍全懌、全端、唐咨、王祚將三萬眾，與文欽同救誕；

translations.literal: When Wu Gang reached Wu, the people of Wu were greatly pleased and sent Generals Quan Yi, Quan Duan, Tang Zi, and Wang Zuo to lead thirty thousand men to join Wen Qin in rescuing Dan;
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Gang reached Wu, the Wu court rejoiced and sent Generals Quan Yi, Quan Duan, Tang Zi, and Wang Zuo with thirty thousand men to join Wen Qin in relieving Shouchun;

sentences.zh: 以誕為左都護、假節、大司徒、驃騎將軍、青州牧，封壽春侯。

translations.literal: Dan was made Left Chief Protector, with provisional authority and staff, Grand Minister over the Masses, General of Agile Cavalry, and Governor of Qingzhou, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan was appointed Left Chief Protector, granted provisional authority and the staff of command, made Grand Minister over the Masses and General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Qingzhou, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 懌，琮之子；

translations.literal: Yi was the son of Cong;
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi was a son of Quan Cong;

sentences.zh: 端，其從子也。

translations.literal: Duan was his nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Duan was his nephew.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲子，車駕次項，司馬昭督諸軍二十六萬進屯丘頭，以鎮南將軍王基行鎮東將軍、都督揚豫諸軍事，與安東將軍陳騫等圍壽春。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jia-zi, the imperial carriage halted at Xiang; Sima Zhao supervised an army of two hundred sixty thousand and advanced to encamp at Qiutou. He appointed General Who Guards the South Wang Ji acting General Who Guards the East and overall commander of military affairs in Yang and Yu, and together with General Who Establishes the East Chen Qian and others besieged Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jia-zi, the Emperor halted at Xiang. Sima Zhao took command of two hundred sixty thousand troops and advanced to Qiutou. He made General Who Guards the South Wang Ji acting General Who Guards the East and overall commander of military affairs in Yang and Yu, and together with General Who Establishes the East Chen Qian and others laid siege to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 基始至，圍城未合，文欽、全懌等從城東北因山乘險，得將其眾突入城。

translations.literal: When Ji had just arrived, the encirclement of the city was not yet closed; Wen Qin, Quan Yi, and the others from the northeast of the city used the mountains to seize advantageous terrain and succeeded in leading their troops in a sudden entry into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji had only just arrived and the encirclement was not yet complete when Wen Qin, Quan Yi, and the others came from the northeast, used the mountainous terrain to their advantage, and broke through into the city with their troops.

sentences.zh: 昭敕基斂軍堅壁。

translations.literal: Zhao ordered Ji to withdraw his army and hold fast behind strong walls.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao ordered Wang Ji to pull back his troops and hold fast behind fortified walls.

sentences.zh: 基累求進討，會吳朱異率三萬人進屯安豐，為文欽外勢，詔基引諸軍轉據北山。

translations.literal: Ji repeatedly asked permission to advance and attack; at that time Wu's Zhu Yi led thirty thousand men forward to encamp at Anfeng, forming outer support for Wen Qin, and an edict ordered Ji to lead the armies to shift and hold the northern hills.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji repeatedly requested leave to advance and attack. Meanwhile Zhu Yi of Wu led thirty thousand men forward to Anfeng to support Wen Qin from outside, and an edict ordered Wang Ji to shift the armies to occupy the northern hills.

sentences.zh: 基謂諸將曰：「今圍壘轉固，兵馬向集，但當精修守備，以待越逸，而更移兵守險，使得放縱，雖有智者，不能善其後矣！

translations.literal: Ji said to the generals: "The encirclement is now growing firm and horses and troops are gathering—one need only carefully strengthen defenses and wait for them to break out in flight. Yet instead we are shifting troops to hold difficult terrain and letting them roam free; even a wise man could not set this right afterward!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji told the generals, "The siege lines are tightening and our forces are assembling. We need only strengthen our defenses and wait for them to attempt a breakout. Shifting troops to hold the high ground instead will give the enemy room to act freely—even the wisest strategist could not salvage matters after that!

sentences.zh: 」遂守便宜，上疏曰：「今與賊家對敵，當不動如山，若遷移依險，人心搖蕩，於勢大損。

translations.literal: " He therefore held to what was expedient and submitted a memorial saying: "We are now facing the enemy's host in battle; we should stand unmoving as a mountain. If we shift and cling to difficult terrain, hearts will sway, and our position will be greatly weakened.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore acted as he saw fit and submitted a memorial: "We face the enemy host head-on and should stand firm as a mountain. If we relocate to hold difficult terrain, morale will falter and our position will suffer a grave setback.

sentences.zh: 諸軍並據深溝高壘，眾心皆定，不可傾動，此御兵之要也。

translations.literal: All the armies together hold deep moats and high ramparts; everyone's heart is settled and must not be shaken—this is the essential principle of commanding troops.
translations.idiomatic: All our armies hold deep trenches and high ramparts; morale is steady and must not be disturbed. That is the essential principle of command.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，報聽。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted and a reply came granting his request.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 於是基等四面合圍，表裡再重，塹壘甚峻。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ji and the others completed the encirclement on all four sides, with inner and outer lines twofold, and moats and ramparts very steep.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wang Ji and the others completed a four-sided encirclement with double inner and outer lines and very steep trenches and ramparts.

sentences.zh: 文欽等數出犯圍，逆擊，走之。

translations.literal: Wen Qin and the others several times came out to violate the encirclement; they were met in counterattack and driven off.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin and his allies sallied out against the siege lines several times but were met in counterattack and driven back.

sentences.zh: 司馬昭又使奮武將軍監青州諸軍事石苞督兗州刺史州泰、徐州刺史胡質等簡銳卒為遊軍，以備外寇。

translations.literal: Sima Zhao also sent General of Inciting Might Shi Bao, overseeing military affairs in Qing Province, to supervise Inspector of Yan Province Zhou Tai, Inspector of Xu Province Hu Zhi, and others in selecting sharp, elite troops to serve as mobile forces against external raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao also sent General of Inciting Might Shi Bao, overseeing military affairs in Qing Province, to supervise Zhou Tai, Inspector of Yanzhou, Hu Zhi, Inspector of Xuzhou, and others in selecting elite troops for a mobile force to guard against outside attack.

sentences.zh: 泰擊破朱異於陽淵，異走，泰追之，殺傷二千人。

translations.literal: Tai defeated Zhu Yi at Yangyuan; Yi fled, Tai pursued him, and killed and wounded two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Tai routed Zhu Yi at Yangyuan. Zhu Yi fled, Zhou Tai pursued him, and killed or wounded two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，吳大將軍綝大發卒出屯鑊裡，復遣朱異帥將軍丁奉、黎斐等五人前解壽春之圍。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Wu's Grand General Chen greatly mobilized troops and went out to encamp at Huoli; he again sent Zhu Yi leading Generals Ding Feng, Li Fei, and five others forward to lift the siege of Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Sun Chen, Wu's Grand General, mobilized a large force and encamped at Huoli. He again sent Zhu Yi at the head of Generals Ding Feng, Li Fei, and five others forward to break the siege of Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 異留輜重於都陸，進屯黎漿，石苞、州泰又擊破之。

translations.literal: Yi left baggage at Dulu and advanced to encamp at Lijiang; Shi Bao and Zhou Tai again defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi left his baggage train at Dulu and advanced to Lijiang, where Shi Bao and Zhou Tai defeated him again.

sentences.zh: 太山太守胡烈以奇兵五千襲都陸，盡焚異資糧，異將餘兵，食葛葉，走歸孫綝。

translations.literal: Taishan Administrator Hu Lie with five thousand picked troops raided Dulu, burned all of Yi's supplies, and Yi led the remaining troops, eating kudzu leaves, and fled back to Sun Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Lie, Administrator of Taishan, raided Dulu with five thousand picked troops and burned all of Zhu Yi's supplies. Zhu Yi led his surviving troops back—living on kudzu leaves—and fled to Sun Chen.

sentences.zh: 綝使異更死戰，異以士卒乏食，不從綝命。

translations.literal: Chen ordered Yi to fight again to the death; Yi, because the officers and soldiers lacked food, did not obey Chen's order.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chen ordered Zhu Yi back into deadly combat, but Zhu Yi, whose troops were starving, refused the order.

sentences.zh: 綝怒，九月，己巳，綝斬異於鑊裡。

translations.literal: Chen was angry; in the ninth month, on ji-si, Chen executed Yi at Huoli.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, in the ninth month on ji-si Sun Chen executed Zhu Yi at Huoli.

sentences.zh: 辛未，引兵還建業，綝既不能拔出諸葛誕，而喪敗士眾，自戮名將，由是吳人莫不怨之。

translations.literal: On xin-wei, he led his army back to Jianye. Chen had neither been able to pull Zhuge Dan out nor avoid losing and defeating troops and men; he had himself killed a famous general—whereupon no one in Wu did not resent him.
translations.idiomatic: On xin-wei he withdrew to Jianye. Sun Chen had failed to relieve Zhuge Dan, lost troops in defeat, and killed a celebrated general himself—whereupon resentment spread across Wu.

sentences.zh: 司馬昭曰：「異不得至壽春，非其罪也，而吳人殺之，欲以謝壽春而堅誕意，使其猶望救耳。

translations.literal: Sima Zhao said: "Yi did not reach Shouchun—it was not his crime—yet the people of Wu killed him, wishing to appease Shouchun and firm Dan's resolve, so that he might still hope for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao said, "Zhu Yi never reached Shouchun—that was not his fault. Yet Wu executed him, hoping to appease Shouchun and steel Zhuge Dan's resolve so he would still cling to hope of rescue.

sentences.zh: 今當堅圍，備其越逸，而多方以誤之。

translations.literal: We should now hold the encirclement firm, guard against their breaking out in flight, and in many ways mislead them.
translations.idiomatic: We must hold the siege tight, guard against a breakout, and mislead them by every means.

sentences.zh: 」乃縱反間，揚言「吳救方至，大軍乏食，分遣羸疾就谷淮北，勢不能久」。

translations.literal: " He then spread counter-intelligence, publicly announcing: "Wu relief is about to arrive; the great army lacks food and is dispatching the weak and sick to gather grain north of the Huai—its strength cannot last long."
translations.idiomatic: " He then spread disinformation, publicly declaring, "Wu reinforcements are about to arrive; the main army is short of food and is sending the weak and sick to gather grain north of the Huai—it cannot hold out much longer."

sentences.zh: 誕等益寬恣食，俄而城中乏糧，外救不至。

translations.literal: Dan and the others became ever more lax and ate freely; before long the city lacked grain and outside relief did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan and his allies grew ever more careless in consuming provisions. Before long the city ran short of grain and no outside relief arrived.

sentences.zh: 將軍蔣班、焦彝，皆誕腹心謀主也，言於誕曰：「朱異等以大眾來而不能進，孫綝殺異而歸江東，外以發兵為名，內實坐須成敗。

translations.literal: Generals Jiang Ban and Jiao Yi were both Dan's trusted inner advisers in planning; they said to Dan: "Zhu Yi and the others came with a great host yet could not advance; Sun Chen killed Yi and returned east of the Yangtze—outwardly in the name of sending troops, inwardly in fact sitting and waiting for success or failure.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Jiang Ban and Jiao Yi, both Zhuge Dan's closest advisers, told him, "Zhu Yi came with a great host and could not break through; Sun Chen executed him and returned to the east of the Yangtze—in name sending troops, but in truth simply waiting to see who would win.

sentences.zh: 今宜及眾心尚固，士卒思用，並力決死，攻其一面，雖不能盡克，猶有可全者；

translations.literal: Now we should take advantage while the people's hearts are still firm and officers and soldiers are eager to fight, unite our strength in a fight to the death, and attack on one front—even if we cannot fully conquer them, there may still be something that can be preserved;
translations.idiomatic: We should act while morale still holds and the troops are eager to fight—unite in a desperate assault on one front. Even if we cannot win outright, something may still be saved;

sentences.zh: 空坐守死，無為也。

translations.literal: to sit empty-handed and guard until death is to accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: to sit passively and wait for death accomplishes nothing.

sentences.zh: 」文欽曰：「公今舉十餘萬之眾歸命於吳，而欽與全端等皆同居死地，父兄子弟盡在江表，就孫綝不欲來，主上及其親戚豈肯聽乎！

translations.literal: " Wen Qin said: "Your Excellency has now brought an army of more than a hundred thousand to submit to Wu; Qin and Quan Duan and the others all share one place of death together—the fathers, elder brothers, sons, and younger brothers are all east of the Yangtze; even if Sun Chen did not wish to come, would the sovereign and his kin consent!
translations.idiomatic: " Wen Qin replied, "Your Excellency has now surrendered more than a hundred thousand men to Wu. Qin, Quan Duan, and the rest of us share the same fate—our fathers, brothers, sons, and kin are all east of the Yangtze. Even if Sun Chen himself had no wish to come, would the sovereign and his kin ever agree!

sentences.zh: 且中國無歲無事，軍民並疲，今守我一年，內變將起，奈何捨此，欲乘危徼幸乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, in the Central State there is no year without affairs; army and people alike are weary. If they hold us under siege for a year, internal turmoil will arise—why abandon this and wish to seize danger for a lucky chance!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Central Plains know no year without crisis—army and people alike are exhausted. Hold us here for a year and internal rebellion will erupt. Why abandon that prospect to gamble on a desperate sortie!

sentences.zh: 」班、彝固勸之，欽怒。

translations.literal: " Ban and Yi still pressed their counsel; Qin grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: " Ban and Yi continued to press their advice; Wen Qin flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 誕欲殺班、彝，二人懼，十一月，棄誕逾城來降。

translations.literal: Dan wished to kill Ban and Yi; the two men feared this, and in the eleventh month they abandoned Dan, crossed the wall, and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan intended to kill Ban and Yi. Fearing for their lives, the two men in the eleventh month abandoned him, climbed over the wall, and defected.

sentences.zh: 全懌兄子輝、儀在建業，與其家內爭訟，攜其母將部曲數十家來奔。

translations.literal: Quan Yi's elder brother's sons Hui and Yi were in Jianye; they had a dispute within the family, took their mother, and led several dozen households of personal troops to come and defect.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi's nephews Hui and Yi were in Jianye. After a dispute within the family, they took their mother and led several dozen households of personal troops across to surrender.

sentences.zh: 於是懌與兄子靖及全端弟翩、緝皆將兵在壽春城中，司馬昭用黃門侍郎鐘會策，密為輝、儀作書，使輝、儀所親信繼入城告懌等，說「吳中怒懌等不能拔壽春，欲盡誅諸將家，故逃來歸命」。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yi and his elder brother's son Jing, and Quan Duan's younger brothers Pian and Ji, were all leading troops inside Shouchun. Sima Zhao used Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gates Zhong Hui's stratagem, secretly drafting letters for Hui and Yi, and sent men trusted by Hui and Yi in succession into the city to tell Yi and the others, saying: "In Wu they are angry that Yi and the others could not lift the siege of Shouchun and wish to execute all the generals' families, so they have fled to submit."
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Quan Yi, his nephew Jing, and Quan Duan's younger brothers Pian and Ji all held troops inside Shouchun. Sima Zhao adopted a stratagem from Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gates Zhong Hui, secretly forged letters in the names of Hui and Yi, and sent their trusted associates into the city to tell Quan Yi and the others, "Wu is furious that Quan Yi and the others failed to relieve Shouchun and intends to execute every general's family—that is why we fled to surrender."

sentences.zh: 十二月，懌等率其眾數千人開門出降，城中震懼，不知所為。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Yi and the others led their several thousand followers to open the gates and come out to surrender; inside the city there was shock and fear, and no one knew what to do.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Quan Yi and his followers—several thousand strong—opened the gates and surrendered. The city was shaken with terror and no one knew what to do.

sentences.zh: 詔拜懌平東將軍，封臨湘侯；

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yi General Who Pacifies the East and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Linxiang;
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Quan Yi General Who Pacifies the East and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Linxiang;

sentences.zh: 端等封拜各有差。

translations.literal: Duan and the others received enfeoffments and appointments each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Duan and the others received titles and appointments according to their rank.

sentences.zh: 漢姜維聞魏分關中兵以赴淮南，欲乘虛向秦川，率數萬人出駱谷，至沈嶺。

translations.literal: Shu's Jiang Wei, hearing that Wei had divided Guanzhong troops to go to Huainan, wished to exploit the opening toward Qinchuan and led several tens of thousands out through Luogu Valley as far as Shenling.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Wei of Shu heard that Wei had diverted Guanzhong troops to Huainan, he sought to exploit the opening and march on Qinchuan, leading tens of thousands out through Luogu Valley to Shenling.

sentences.zh: 時長城積穀甚多，而守兵少，征西將軍都督雍、涼諸軍事司馬望及安西將軍鄧艾進兵據之，以拒維。

translations.literal: At the time Changcheng had much accumulated grain but few defenders; Western Campaign General and commander of military affairs in Yong and Liang Sima Wang and Anxi General Deng Ai advanced to occupy it and resist Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Changcheng held large grain stores but few defenders. Western Campaign General Sima Wang, commander of Yong and Liang, and Anxi General Deng Ai advanced to seize it and block Jiang Wei.

sentences.zh: 維壁於芒水，數挑戰，望、艾不應。

translations.literal: Wei fortified at the Mang River and repeatedly offered battle; Wang and Ai did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Wei fortified along the Mang River and repeatedly challenged them to battle, but Wang and Ai would not engage.

sentences.zh: 是時，維數出兵，蜀人愁苦。

translations.literal: At this time Wei campaigned repeatedly and the people of Shu were worn with distress.
translations.idiomatic: By then Jiang Wei was campaigning again and again, and the people of Shu were worn down with hardship.

sentences.zh: 中散大夫譙周作《仇國論》以諷之曰：「或問往古能以弱勝強者，其術如何？

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Qiao Zhou wrote "Treatise on a Feudatory State" to admonish him, saying: "Someone asked: In antiquity those who could use weakness to overcome strength—what was their method?
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Qiao Zhou wrote "Treatise on a Feudatory State" to admonish him, saying, "Someone asked how, in antiquity, the weak overcame the strong. What was their method?

sentences.zh: 曰：吾聞之，處大無患者常多慢，處小有憂者常思善；

translations.literal: The answer was: I have heard that those in a large state without troubles are often negligent, while those in a small state with worries often think of what is good;
translations.idiomatic: The answer was: I have heard that great states without troubles grow negligent, while small states under pressure think constantly of improvement;

sentences.zh: 多慢則生亂，思善則生治，理之常也。

translations.literal: much negligence breeds disorder, much thought of good breeds order—this is the constant principle of things.
translations.idiomatic: negligence breeds disorder, and striving for good breeds order. That is the constant way of things.

sentences.zh: 故周文養民，以少取多，勾踐恤眾，以弱斃強，此其術也。

translations.literal: Therefore King Wen of Zhou nourished the people and with few took many; Goujian cared for the masses and with weak destroyed strong—this was their method.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen of Zhou nourished his people and with the few overcame the many; Goujian of Yue cared for his people and with the weak destroyed the strong. That was their method.

sentences.zh: 或曰：曩者，項強漢弱，相與戰爭，項羽與漢約分鴻溝，各歸息民，張良以為民志既定，則難動也，率兵追羽，終斃項氏。

translations.literal: Someone said: Formerly Xiang was strong and Han weak; they fought each other. Xiang Yu and Han agreed to divide at the Hong Canal and each return to rest the people. Zhang Liang thought that once the people's will was settled it would be hard to move them; he led troops in pursuit of Yu and finally destroyed the Xiang clan.
translations.idiomatic: But someone objected: Once Xiang Yu was strong and Han weak. They fought until Xiang Yu and Han agreed to divide at the Hong Canal and each return to rest their people. Zhang Liang argued that once the people's will had settled it would be hard to move them again; he led troops in pursuit and finally destroyed the house of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 豈必由文王之事乎？

translations.literal: Must this necessarily follow the affairs of King Wen?
translations.idiomatic: Must victory always follow the way of King Wen?

sentences.zh: 曰：當商、周之際，王侯世尊，君臣久固，民習所專；

translations.literal: The answer was: At the time of Shang and Zhou, kings and marquises were held in honor, lord and minister were long established, and the people were accustomed to their allegiance;
translations.idiomatic: The answer was: In the age of Shang and Zhou, kings and feudal lords were deeply honored, lord and minister bonds were long settled, and the people were rooted in their allegiances;

sentences.zh: 深根者難拔，據固者難遷。

translations.literal: those deeply rooted are hard to uproot, those firmly established are hard to displace.
translations.idiomatic: those deeply rooted are hard to uproot, and those firmly established are hard to displace.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，雖漢祖安能杖劍鞭馬而取天下乎！

translations.literal: At such a time, how could even Han's founder have seized the realm by brandishing a sword and whipping his horse!
translations.idiomatic: In such an age, how could even Han's founder have seized the realm by sword and spur alone!

sentences.zh: 及秦罷侯置守之後，民疲秦役，天下土崩，或歲改主，或月易公，鳥驚獸駭，莫知所從，於是豪強並爭，虎裂狼分，疾搏者獲多，遲後者見吞。

translations.literal: After Qin abolished the feudal lords and set up commandery governors, the people were worn by Qin corvée, the realm collapsed, rulers changed by the year or lords by the month; birds were startled and beasts terrified, none knew whom to follow—then the powerful contended together, tigers tore and wolves divided; the swift in battle gained much, the slow were swallowed.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin abolished the feudal lords and installed commandery governors, the people were exhausted by Qin labor, and the realm collapsed. Rulers changed yearly, lords monthly. Birds scattered and beasts panicked, and no one knew whom to follow. Then the powerful contended; tigers tore and wolves divided the land. The swift in battle gained much, and the slow were swallowed.

sentences.zh: 今我與彼皆傳國易世矣，既非秦末鼎沸之時，實有六國並據之勢，故可為文王，難為漢祖。

translations.literal: Now we and they have both transmitted states through many generations; it is no longer the seething end of Qin, but truly has the aspect of the Six States holding territory side by side—therefore one can be a King Wen, but it is hard to be a Han founder.
translations.idiomatic: Now we and they have both been established states for generations. This is no longer the seething chaos at the end of Qin, but truly resembles the age when the Six States held their ground side by side. One may act like King Wen, but it is hard to act like Han's founder.

sentences.zh: 夫民之疲勞，則騷擾之兆生，上慢下暴，則瓦解之形起。

translations.literal: When the people are worn with labor, the omens of unrest arise; when those above are negligent and those below violent, the pattern of collapse appears.
translations.idiomatic: When the people are worn with labor, unrest follows. When those above grow negligent and those below grow violent, collapse begins.

sentences.zh: 諺曰：『射幸數跌，不如審發。

translations.literal: A proverb says: 'Relying on luck in shooting, one often misses; better to aim carefully.
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb says, "Hoping for luck in archery, one often misses; better to aim carefully.

sentences.zh: 』是故智者不為小利移目，不為意似改步，時可而後動，數合而後舉，故湯、武之師不再戰而克，誠重民勞而度時審也。

translations.literal: ' Therefore the wise do not shift their gaze for small profit, do not change their step for seeming opportunity; they move when the time is right and act when conditions align—thus the armies of Tang and Wu conquered without fighting again, truly weighing the people's labor and judging the time carefully.
translations.idiomatic: " Therefore the wise do not chase small gains or change course on a whim. They move when the time is right and act when conditions align. That is why the armies of Tang and Wu conquered without needing to fight again: they weighed the people's labor and judged the moment carefully.

sentences.zh: 如遂極武黷征，土崩勢生，不幸遇難，雖有智者，將不能謀之矣。

translations.literal: If one then exhausts martial force in repeated campaigns, the trend of collapse arises; should misfortune be encountered, even if there were a wise man, he could not devise a remedy.
translations.idiomatic: If one then exhausts the state in repeated campaigns, collapse follows. Should disaster strike, even a wise adviser could not save it.

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公下甘露三年（

translations.literal: Under the Duke of Gaoguixiang, third year of Ganlu (
translations.idiomatic: Under the Duke of Gaoguixiang, third year of Ganlu (

sentences.zh: 戊寅，公元二五八年）

translations.literal: wuyin, AD 258)
translations.idiomatic: the year wuyin, AD 258)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，文欽謂諸葛誕曰：「蔣班、焦彝謂我不能出而走，全端、全懌又率眾逆降，此敵無備之時也，可以戰矣。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, Wen Qin said to Zhuge Dan: "Jiang Ban and Jiao Yi said I could not hold out and fled; Quan Duan and Quan Yi have also led their men in surrender to the enemy—this is a time when the foe is unprepared; we can fight.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Wen Qin said to Zhuge Dan, "Jiang Ban and Jiao Yi said I could not endure and fled. Quan Duan and Quan Yi have led their men in surrender to the enemy. The foe is unprepared—we can fight.

sentences.zh: 」誕及唐咨等皆以為然，遂大為攻具，晝夜五六日攻南圍，欲決圍而出。

translations.literal: " Dan and Tang Zi and the others all agreed; they therefore built siege engines on a large scale and for five or six days and nights assaulted the southern encirclement, wishing to break out.
translations.idiomatic: " Dan, Tang Zi, and the others agreed. They built siege engines on a large scale and for five or six days and nights assaulted the southern siege line, trying to break out.

sentences.zh: 圍上諸軍臨高發石車火箭，逆燒破其攻具，矢石雨下，死傷蔽地，血流盈塹，復不城。

translations.literal: The besieging armies from the heights launched stone-throwing engines and fire-arrows, burned and destroyed their siege works in counterattack; arrows and stones fell like rain, the dead and wounded covered the ground, blood filled the moats, and they did not take the wall.
translations.idiomatic: The besieging armies on the heights launched catapults and fire-arrows, burned their siege works, and rained missiles down. The dead and wounded covered the ground, blood filled the moats, and they failed to break the line.

sentences.zh: 城內食轉竭，出降者數萬口。

translations.literal: Food within the city grew ever scarcer; those who came out to surrender numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Food inside the city ran ever lower, and tens of thousands came out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 欽欲盡出北方人，省食，與吳人堅守，誕不聽，由是爭恨。

translations.literal: Qin wished to send out all the northerners to save food and hold firm with the Wu men; Dan would not listen, and from this they quarreled in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Qin wanted to expel all the northerners to save food and hold the city with the Wu troops alone. Dan refused, and they grew bitter toward each other.

sentences.zh: 欽素與誕有隙，徒以計合，事急愈相疑。

translations.literal: Qin and Dan had long had a rift; they had joined only by calculation, and as the crisis deepened they suspected each other all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Dan had long been at odds and had joined only by calculation. As the crisis deepened, their mutual suspicion grew.

sentences.zh: 欽見誕計事，誕遂殺欽。

translations.literal: When Qin came to discuss plans with Dan, Dan thereupon killed Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin came to discuss plans, Dan killed him.

sentences.zh: 欽子鴦、虎將兵在小城中，聞欽死，勒兵赴之；

translations.literal: Qin's sons Yang and Hu commanded troops in a small inner citadel; hearing of Qin's death, they mustered their men to go to him;
translations.idiomatic: Qin's sons Yang and Hu held troops in an inner citadel. Hearing of their father's death, they mustered their men to rush to the scene;

sentences.zh: 眾不為用，遂單走逾城出，自歸於司馬昭。

translations.literal: the troops would not obey, so they fled alone over the wall and surrendered themselves to Sima Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: but the troops would not follow. They fled alone over the wall and surrendered to Sima Zhao.

sentences.zh: 軍吏請誅之，昭曰：「欽之罪不容誅，其子固應就戮；

translations.literal: The military officers asked to execute them; Zhao said: "Qin's crime admits no sparing, and his sons ought indeed to be put to death;
translations.idiomatic: The officers asked to execute them. Zhao said, "Qin's crime admits no sparing, and his sons would ordinarily deserve death;

sentences.zh: 然鴦、虎以窮歸命，且城未拔，殺之是堅其心也。

translations.literal: yet Yang and Hu have come in submission at their extremity, and the city is not yet taken—killing them would harden the hearts of those within.
translations.idiomatic: yet Yang and Hu have surrendered in desperation, and the city is not yet taken. Killing them would only harden the hearts of those inside.

sentences.zh: 」乃赦鴦、虎，使將數百騎巡城，呼曰：「文欽之子猶不見殺，其餘何懼！

translations.literal: " He therefore pardoned Yang and Hu and had them lead several hundred horsemen around the wall, calling out: "Even Wen Qin's sons are not killed—what have the rest to fear!
translations.idiomatic: " He pardoned Yang and Hu and had them lead several hundred horsemen around the wall, calling out, "Even Wen Qin's sons are not killed—what have the rest to fear!

sentences.zh: 」又表鴦、虎皆為將軍，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized that Yang and Hu should both be made generals and granted the rank of Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: " He also memorialized that Yang and Hu should be made generals and granted the rank of Marquis within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 城內皆喜，且日益饑困。

translations.literal: Those within the city were all pleased, yet hunger and distress grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Those inside the city were heartened, even as hunger and distress grew daily.

sentences.zh: 司馬昭身自臨圍，見城上持弓者不發，曰：「可攻矣！

translations.literal: Sima Zhao personally came to the siege; seeing those on the wall holding bows but not shooting, he said: "It can be attacked!
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao came in person to the siege. Seeing archers on the wall who would not shoot, he said, "It can be taken now!

sentences.zh: 」乃四面進軍，同時鼓噪登城。

translations.literal: " He then advanced on all four sides, and at the same time with drums and shouts scaled the wall.
translations.idiomatic: " He then advanced on all four sides, and at once, with drums and shouts, his men scaled the walls.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙酉，克之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on yiyou, it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day yiyou, the city fell.

sentences.zh: 誕窘急，單馬將其麾下突小城欲出，司馬胡奮部兵擊斬之，夷其三族。

translations.literal: Dan in desperate straits, alone on horseback leading his followers in a dash through the small citadel wishing to escape, was struck down and beheaded by the troops of Major Hu Fen; his clan was exterminated to the third degree.
translations.idiomatic: Dan, in desperate straits, rode alone at the head of his followers through the inner citadel trying to escape. Major Hu Fen's troops struck him down and beheaded him, and his clan was exterminated to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 誕麾下數百人，皆拱手為列，不降，每斬一人，輒降之，卒不變，以至於盡。

translations.literal: Several hundred of Dan's followers stood with hands clasped in ranks and would not surrender; for each one beheaded, another would submit, yet in the end none changed, until all were gone.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred of Dan's followers stood with clasped hands in ranks and would not surrender. For each man beheaded, another would submit, yet in the end none yielded, until all were gone.

sentences.zh: 吳將於詮曰：「大丈夫受命其主，以兵救人，既不能克，又束手於敵，吾弗取也。

translations.literal: Wu general Yu Quan said: "A great man receives his lord's commission and takes arms to save others; if he cannot succeed and then submits bound to the enemy, I will not do that.
translations.idiomatic: Wu general Yu Quan said, "A great man receives his lord's commission and takes up arms to save others. If he cannot succeed and then submits bound to the enemy, I will not do that.

sentences.zh: 」乃免冑冒陳而死。

translations.literal: " He then removed his helmet and charged the battle line to his death.
translations.idiomatic: " He removed his helmet and charged the enemy line to his death.

sentences.zh: 唐咨、王祚等皆降。

translations.literal: Tang Zi, Wang Zuo, and the others all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zi, Wang Zuo, and the others all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 吳兵萬眾，器仗山積。

translations.literal: Wu troops numbered in the tens of thousands; weapons and armor piled like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Wu troops numbered in the tens of thousands, and weapons and armor piled like mountains.

sentences.zh: 司馬昭初圍壽春，王基、石苞等皆欲急攻之，昭以為「壽春城固而眾多，攻之必力屈；

translations.literal: When Sima Zhao first besieged Shouchun, Wang Ji, Shi Bao, and the others all wished to attack urgently; Zhao held that "Shouchun's walls are strong and its defenders many—an assault would surely exhaust our strength;
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhao first besieged Shouchun, Wang Ji, Shi Bao, and the others all wanted a swift assault. Zhao argued, "Shouchun's walls are strong and its defenders many. A direct assault would exhaust our strength;

sentences.zh: 若有外寇，表裡受敵，此危道也。

translations.literal: if there were an external enemy, we would be attacked from within and without—this is a perilous course.
translations.idiomatic: if an outside enemy came, we would be caught between two foes. That would be perilous.

sentences.zh: 今三叛相聚於孤城之中，天其或者使同就戮，吾當以全策縻之。

translations.literal: Now the three rebels are gathered in a lone city—Heaven perhaps intends that they perish together; I should use a strategy of containment to hold them fast.
translations.idiomatic: Now the three rebels are gathered in one isolated city. Heaven perhaps means them to perish together. I should contain them with a strategy of encirclement.

sentences.zh: 但堅守三面，若吳賊陸道而來，軍糧必少；

translations.literal: Only hold firm on three sides; if Wu bandits come by land, their army grain must be scant;
translations.idiomatic: Hold firm on three sides only. If Wu comes by land, their supplies must be limited;

sentences.zh: 吾以遊兵輕騎絕其轉輸，可不戰而破也。

translations.literal: with roaming troops and light cavalry I will cut off their transport—it can be broken without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: I will send roaming troops and light cavalry to cut off their supply lines. We can destroy them without giving battle.

sentences.zh: 吳賊破，欽等必成擒矣！

translations.literal: When Wu bandits are broken, Qin and the others will surely be captured entirely!
translations.idiomatic: Once the Wu forces are broken, Wen Qin and the others will surely be taken without fail!

sentences.zh: 」乃命諸軍按甲以守之，卒不煩攻而破。

translations.literal: " He then ordered the armies to hold their armor and stand on the defensive; in the end he broke them without troubling to attack.
translations.idiomatic: With that, he ordered the armies to hold their positions and stand on the defensive. In the end the rebels were broken without the need for a full assault.

sentences.zh: 議者又以為「淮南仍為叛逆，吳兵室家在江南，不可縱，宜悉坑之。

translations.literal: The deliberators again held that "Huainan remains rebellious; Wu troops' families and homes are south of the Yangtze—they cannot be released; all should be executed in burial pits.
translations.idiomatic: Some at council again argued, "Huainan remains rebel territory, and these Wu soldiers have wives and homes south of the Yangtze. They cannot be let go—all should be put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 」昭曰：「古之用兵，全國為上，戮其元惡而已。

translations.literal: " Zhao said: "In ancient use of troops, to preserve the whole state is highest; only slay the chief villains.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao replied, "In warfare of old, the highest aim was to preserve the whole state; one need only execute the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 吳兵就得亡還，適可以示中國之大度耳。

translations.literal: Wu troops need only be allowed to flee and return—this aptly can show the Middle Kingdom's great magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Wu soldiers flee home. That will aptly demonstrate the magnanimity of the Central Plains."

sentences.zh: 」一無所殺，分佈三河近郡以安處之。

translations.literal: " Not one was killed; they were distributed among the near counties of the three rivers to settle and place them.
translations.idiomatic: Not a single man was killed. They were distributed among counties near the three Huai river systems and settled there in peace.

sentences.zh: 拜唐咨安遠將軍，其餘裨將，鹹假位號，眾皆悅服，其淮南將士吏民為誕所脅略者，皆赦之。

translations.literal: Tang Zi was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance; the remaining subordinate generals—all were granted ranks and titles; the masses all submitted gladly; Huainan officers, soldiers, clerks, and people who had been coerced and plundered by Dan—all were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zi was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance; the remaining subordinate commanders were all granted ranks and titles, and the troops submitted willingly. All Huainan officers, soldiers, officials, and commoners who had been coerced by Zhuge Dan were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 聽文鴦兄弟收斂父喪。

translations.literal: Wen Yang and his brothers were permitted to gather and bury their father's remains.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yang and his brothers were permitted to recover their father's body for burial.

sentences.zh: 給其車牛，致葬舊墓。

translations.literal: Carts and oxen were supplied to them; burial was conducted at the old tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Carts and oxen were provided so that the body might be borne to the family tomb for burial.

sentences.zh: 昭遺王基書曰：「初議者云云，求移者甚眾，時未臨履，亦謂宜然。

translations.literal: Zhao sent a letter to Wang Ji saying: "At first the deliberators talked this way and that; those seeking to shift position were very many; the moment had not yet come to act—and I too thought it should be so.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao wrote to Wang Ji, saying, "At first the council debated endlessly, and many urged shifting our dispositions. The moment had not yet arrived to act, and I too believed they were right.

sentences.zh: 將軍深算利害，獨秉固志，上違詔命，下拒眾議，終至制敵禽賊，雖古人所述，不是過也。

translations.literal: The general calculated deeply the gains and losses, alone held a firm resolve, above defying the imperial edict, below rejecting the multitude's counsel—ultimately subduing the enemy and capturing the bandits; though the ancients described such things, this was no less.
translations.idiomatic: You calculated deeply the gains and losses, held firm to your own resolve, defied the imperial edict above and rejected the counsel of the multitude below—and in the end subdued the enemy and captured the rebels. Even the greatest deeds described by the ancients were no more than this.

sentences.zh: 」昭欲遣諸軍輕兵深入，招迎唐咨等子弟，因釁有滅吳之勢。

translations.literal: " Zhao wished to send the armies' light troops deep in, to summon and welcome Tang Zi's sons and younger brothers, thereby creating an opportunity with momentum to destroy Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao then planned to send light forces deep into enemy territory to summon Tang Zi's sons and kin, thereby creating an opening with momentum toward the destruction of Wu.

sentences.zh: 王基諫曰：「昔諸葛恪乘東關之勝，竭江表之兵以圍新城，城既不拔，而眾死者太半。

translations.literal: Wang Ji remonstrated, saying: "Formerly Zhuge Ke, riding the victory at Dong Gate, exhausted the armies south of the Yangtze to besiege Xincheng; the city was not taken, yet more than half the host perished.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji remonstrated, saying, "In the past Zhuge Ke, riding the victory at Dong Gate, mustered every soldier south of the Yangtze to besiege Xincheng. The city was not taken, and more than half his army was lost.

sentences.zh: 姜維因洮西之利，輕兵深入，糧餉不繼，軍覆上邽。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei, taking advantage of the gains at Taoxi, sent light troops deep in; grain and provisions did not follow, and the army was destroyed at Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei, exploiting the advantage at Taoxi, sent light forces deep into enemy territory, but supplies failed to keep pace and his army was destroyed at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 夫大捷之後，上下輕敵，輕敵則慮難不深。

translations.literal: After a great victory, superiors and inferiors alike despise the enemy; despising the enemy, one does not consider difficulties deeply.
translations.idiomatic: After a great victory, commanders and men alike grow contemptuous of the enemy; and when one despises the enemy, one does not reckon deeply with hardship.

sentences.zh: 今賊新敗於外，又內患未弭，是其修備設慮之時也。

translations.literal: Now the bandits have newly been defeated abroad, and internal troubles are not yet quelled—this is the time when they repair defenses and lay plans.
