translations.idiomatic: Now the enemy has just been defeated in the field, and their internal troubles are not yet settled. This is precisely the moment when they will fortify their defenses and lay their plans.

sentences.zh: 且兵出逾年，人有歸志，今俘馘十萬，罪人斯得，自歷代征伐，未有全兵獨克如今之盛者也。

translations.literal: Moreover the troops have been in the field more than a year; men have thoughts of returning home. Now one hundred thousand captives have been taken and the guilty obtained—in successive generations of campaigning, never has there been a complete army achieving victory alone as magnificent as today.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover our army has been in the field for more than a year, and the men long for home. We have already taken a hundred thousand captives and brought the guilty to justice. In all the campaigns of past ages, never has a whole army won so complete a victory as this.

sentences.zh: 武皇帝克袁紹於官渡，自以所獲已多，不復追奔，懼挫威也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu overcame Yuan Shao at Guandu; he himself considered what he had gained already ample, and did not again pursue the fugitives, fearing to blunt his prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu defeated Yuan Shao at Guandu, yet even he judged his gains sufficient and did not pursue further, fearing to squander his prestige.

sentences.zh: 」昭乃止，以基為征東將軍、都督揚州諸軍事，進封東武侯。

translations.literal: " Zhao then stopped; he made Ji General Who Subdues the East and Area Commander of all military affairs in Yang Province, and advanced him to Marquis of Dongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao thereupon desisted. He appointed Wang Ji General Who Subdues the East and Area Commander of all military affairs in Yang Province, and advanced him to Marquis of Dongwu.

sentences.zh: ══習鑿齒曰：君子謂司馬大將軍於是役也，可謂能以德攻矣。

translations.literal: ══ Xi Zuochi said: The gentleman holds that Grand General Sima in this campaign may be said to have been able to attack with virtue.
translations.idiomatic: ══ Xi Zuochi remarked: The wise hold that Grand General Sima in this campaign may be said to have conquered through virtue.

sentences.zh: 夫建業者異道，各有所尚而不能兼併也。

translations.literal: Those who establish dominion follow different paths; each has what he esteems and cannot combine them all.
translations.idiomatic: Those who build empires follow different paths; each honors one principle and cannot embrace them all at once.

sentences.zh: 故窮武之雄，斃於不仁；

translations.literal: Thus the hero of absolute martial force perishes through lack of benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the champion of sheer martial force perishes through want of benevolence;

sentences.zh: 存義之國，喪於懦退。

translations.literal: the state that preserves righteousness perishes through timid retreat.
translations.idiomatic: and the state founded on righteousness perishes through timid retreat.

sentences.zh: 今一征而禽三叛，大虜吳眾，席捲淮浦，俘馘十萬，可謂壯矣。

translations.literal: Now in one campaign he captured the three rebels, took the great host of Wu, swept the banks of the Huai, and seized a hundred thousand captives—this may be called magnificent.
translations.idiomatic: Now in a single campaign he captured the three rebels, took the great host of Wu, swept the banks of the Huai, and seized a hundred thousand captives—magnificent indeed.

sentences.zh: 而未及安坐，賞王基之功；

translations.literal: Yet before he had even settled to sit at ease, he rewarded Wang Ji's achievement;
translations.idiomatic: Yet before he had even settled into his seat of victory, he rewarded Wang Ji's achievement;

sentences.zh: 種惠吳人，結異類之情；

translations.literal: he planted kindness among Wu people, binding the feelings of a different kind;
translations.idiomatic: he sowed kindness among the people of Wu, winning the hearts of a foreign people;

sentences.zh: 寵鴦葬欽，忘疇昔之隙；

translations.literal: he favored Yang and buried Qin, forgetting the rancor of former days;
translations.idiomatic: he honored Wen Yang and buried Wen Qin, forgetting the grudges of former days;

sentences.zh: 不咎誕眾，使揚土懷愧。

translations.literal: he did not punish Zhuge Dan's multitude, making the lands of Yang bear shame.
translations.idiomatic: he did not punish Zhuge Dan's followers, leaving the people of Yang Province to feel shame rather than hatred.

sentences.zh: 功高而人樂其成，業廣而敵懷其德。

translations.literal: Merit was high and men rejoiced in his success; his enterprise was broad and enemies cherished his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was so great that men rejoiced in his success; his enterprise so broad that even his enemies respected his virtue.

sentences.zh: 武昭既敷，文算又洽，推此道也，天下其孰能當之哉！

translations.literal: Military brilliance was already spread abroad, and civil calculation was also complete—push this way forward, and who under Heaven could withstand him!
translations.idiomatic: His military brilliance was already manifest, and his political calculation fully in accord. Who under Heaven could withstand a man who pursued power in this fashion?

sentences.zh: 司馬昭之克壽春，鐘會謀畫居多；

translations.literal: In Sima Zhao's capture of Shouchun, Zhong Hui's planning and scheming counted for the greater part;
translations.idiomatic: In Sima Zhao's capture of Shouchun, Zhong Hui's planning counted for the greater part;

sentences.zh: 昭親待日隆，委以腹心之任，時人比之子房。

translations.literal: Zhao personally treated him with increasing favor and entrusted him with duties of the innermost heart; men of the time compared him to Zifang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao treated him with ever greater personal favor and entrusted him with duties at the very center of power; contemporaries compared him to Zhang Liang.

sentences.zh: 漢姜維聞諸葛誕死，退還成都，復拜大將軍。

translations.literal: Shu's Jiang Wei, hearing that Zhuge Dan had died, withdrew and returned to Chengdu; he was again appointed Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Wei of Shu heard that Zhuge Dan was dead, he withdrew to Chengdu and was again appointed Grand General.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，詔以司馬昭為相國，封晉公，食邑八郡，加九錫；

translations.literal: In summer, in the fifth month, an edict appointed Sima Zhao Chancellor of State, enfeoffed him as Duke of Jin with a fief of eight commanderies, and granted the Nine Bestowments;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fifth month, an edict appointed Sima Zhao Chancellor of State, enfeoffed him as Duke of Jin with a fief of eight commanderies, and granted him the Nine Bestowments;

sentences.zh: 昭前後九讓，乃止。

translations.literal: Zhao declined nine times before and after, and then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao declined nine times in all, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，吳主封故齊王奮為章安侯。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, the ruler of Wu enfeoffed the former Prince of Qi, Fen, as Marquis of Zhang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, the ruler of Wu enfeoffed the former Prince of Qi, Sun Fen, as Marquis of Zhang'an.

sentences.zh: 八月，以驃騎將軍王昶為司空。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Flying Cavalry General Wang Chang was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Flying Cavalry General Wang Chang was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 詔以關內侯王祥為三老，鄭小同為五更，帝率群臣幸太學，行養老乞言之禮。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Marquis Within the Passes Wang Xiang as Elder of the Three, and Zheng Xiaotong as Elder of the Five; the Emperor led the ministers to the Imperial Academy and performed the rites of nurturing the aged and seeking counsel.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Marquis Within the Passes Wang Xiang as Elder of the Three and Zheng Xiaotong as Elder of the Five; the emperor led his ministers to the Imperial Academy and performed the rites of nurturing the aged and seeking counsel.

sentences.zh: 小同，玄之孫也。

translations.literal: Xiaotong was the grandson of Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong was the grandson of Zheng Xuan.

sentences.zh: 吳孫綝以吳主親覽政事，多所難問，甚懼；

translations.literal: Wu's Sun Chen, because the ruler of Wu personally reviewed government affairs and often questioned him sharply, was greatly afraid;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chen of Wu, finding that the emperor personally reviewed affairs of state and often questioned him sharply, was greatly afraid;

sentences.zh: 返自鑊裡，遂稱疾不朝，使弟威遠將軍據入倉龍門宿衛，武衛將軍恩、偏將軍干、長水校尉闓分屯諸營，欲以自固。

translations.literal: returning from Huoli, he then claimed illness and did not attend court; he sent his younger brother, General Who Overawes the Distance Ju, to enter and garrison Canglong Gate as palace guard; Military Guard General En, Assistant General Gan, and Colonel of the Changshui Regiment Kai were stationed separately at the various camps, intending thereby to fortify himself.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from Huoli he claimed illness and stopped attending court. He posted his younger brother Ju, General Who Overawes the Distance, to garrison Canglong Gate as palace guard, while Military Guard General En, Assistant General Gan, and Colonel of the Changshui Regiment Kai were stationed at separate camps—all to strengthen his own position.

sentences.zh: 吳主惡之，乃推朱公主死意，全公主懼曰：「我實不知，皆朱據二子熊、損所白。

translations.literal: The ruler of Wu hated this; he then pressed the matter of Princess Zhu's death; Princess Quan, in fear, said: "I truly did not know—it was all reported by Zhu Ju's two sons Xiong and Sun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hated this. He pressed the investigation into Princess Zhu's death, and Princess Quan, in fear, said, "I truly knew nothing of it—it was all reported by Zhu Ju's two sons, Xiong and Sun.

sentences.zh: 」是時熊為虎林督、損為外部督，吳主皆殺之。

translations.literal: " At this time Xiong was Supervisor of Hulin and Sun was External Supervisor; the ruler of Wu killed them both.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiong was Supervisor of Hulin and Sun was External Supervisor; the emperor had them both executed.

sentences.zh: 損妻，即孫峻妹也。

translations.literal: Sun's wife was the younger sister of Sun Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Sun's wife was the younger sister of Sun Jun.

sentences.zh: 綝諫，不從，由是益懼。

translations.literal: Chen remonstrated, but the ruler would not listen; thereby he grew still more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chen remonstrated, but the emperor would not listen, and Chen grew still more afraid.

sentences.zh: 吳主陰與全公主及將軍劉丞謀誅綝。

translations.literal: The ruler of Wu secretly joined Princess Quan and General Liu Cheng in a plot to execute Chen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly joined Empress Quan and General Liu Cheng in a plot to kill Sun Chen.

sentences.zh: 全后父尚為太常、衛將軍，吳主謂尚子黃門侍郎紀曰：「孫綝專勢，輕小於孤。

translations.literal: Empress Quan's father Shang was Grand Minister of Ceremonials and Guard General; the ruler of Wu said to Shang's son, Yellow Gate Attendant Ji: "Sun Chen monopolizes power and treats me lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Quan's father, Quan Shang, was Grand Minister of Ceremonials and Guard General. The emperor said to Shang's son, Yellow Gate Attendant Quan Ji, "Sun Chen monopolizes power and treats me with contempt.

sentences.zh: 孤前敕之使速上岸，為唐咨等作援，而留湖中不上岸一步；

translations.literal: I formerly ordered him to come ashore quickly to aid Tang Zi and the others, yet he remained on the lake and did not take one step ashore;
translations.idiomatic: I once ordered him to come ashore at once to support Tang Zi and the others, yet he stayed on the lake and would not take one step onto land;

sentences.zh: 又委罪於朱異，擅殺功臣，不先表聞；

translations.literal: again he shifted blame onto Zhu Yi and on his own authority killed a meritorious minister, without first reporting to the throne;
translations.idiomatic: he shifted blame onto Zhu Yi and on his own authority killed a meritorious minister without first reporting to me;

sentences.zh: 築第橋南，不復朝見。

translations.literal: he built a mansion south of the Bridge and no longer attended court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: he built a mansion south of the Bridge and no longer came to court.

sentences.zh: 此為自在，無復所畏，不可久忍，今規取之。

translations.literal: In this he acts as he pleases and fears nothing; this cannot long be endured—now I plan to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: He does as he pleases and fears nothing. This cannot be endured any longer. I mean to seize him now.

sentences.zh: 卿父作中軍都督，使密嚴整士馬，孤當自出臨橋，率宿衛虎騎、左右無難一時圍之，作版詔敕絲林所領皆解散，不得舉手。

translations.literal: Your father shall serve as Area Commander of the Central Army; have him secretly drill and ready troops and horses. I shall personally go out to the Bridge, leading the palace guard Tiger Cavalry and the Left and Right Wunans to surround him at once; I shall issue an edict on bamboo ordering all troops under Sun Chen's command to disband and not raise a hand.
translations.idiomatic: Your father will serve as Area Commander of the Central Army. Have him secretly drill the troops and horses. I shall go out to the Bridge in person, leading the palace guard Tiger Cavalry and the Left and Right Wunans to surround him at once, and issue an edict ordering all troops under Sun Chen's command to disband and not lift a hand.

sentences.zh: 正爾，自當得之；

translations.literal: Just so, we shall naturally obtain him;
translations.idiomatic: Do that, and we shall take him without fail;

sentences.zh: 卿去，但當使密耳！

translations.literal: you go—but only keep it secret!
translations.idiomatic: Go now—but tell no one!

sentences.zh: 卿宣詔卿父，勿令卿母知之；

translations.literal: You shall announce the edict to your father; do not let your mother know;
translations.idiomatic: Carry the edict to your father, but do not let your mother know;

sentences.zh: 女人既不曉大事，且綝同堂姊，邂逅漏洩，誤孤非小也！

translations.literal: women do not understand great affairs, and moreover Chen is her cousin on the father's side—a chance leak would be no small harm to me!
translations.idiomatic: women do not understand affairs of state, and Chen is her cousin on her father's side. A chance leak would ruin everything!

sentences.zh: 」紀承詔以告尚。

translations.literal: " Ji received the edict and told Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji received the edict and told Quan Shang.

sentences.zh: 尚無遠慮，以語紀母，母使人密語綝。

translations.literal: Shang had no far-reaching thought; he told Ji's mother, and the mother sent someone to tell Chen secretly.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Shang lacked foresight and told Ji's mother, who sent word secretly to Sun Chen.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊午，綝夜以兵襲尚，執之，遣弟恩殺劉承於蒼龍門外，比明，遂圍宮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day wuwu, Chen by night sent troops to attack Shang, seized him, and dispatched his younger brother En to kill Liu Cheng outside Canglong Gate; by dawn he had surrounded the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day wuwu, Sun Chen attacked Quan Shang by night, seized him, and sent his younger brother En to kill Liu Cheng outside Canglong Gate. By dawn he had surrounded the palace.

sentences.zh: 吳主大怒，上馬帶□建執弓欲出，曰：「孤大皇帝適子，在位已五年，誰敢不從者！

translations.literal: The ruler of Wu was greatly enraged; he mounted his horse, girded himself, grasped a bow, and wished to go out, saying: "I am the legitimate son of the Grand Emperor; I have held the throne five years—who would dare not obey!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. He mounted his horse, girded on his arms, took up his bow, and tried to ride out, crying, "I am the Grand Emperor's legitimate heir. I have reigned five years—who would dare disobey me!

sentences.zh: 」侍中近臣及乳母共牽攀止之，不得出，歎吒不食，罵全后曰：「爾父憒憒，敗我大事！

translations.literal: " Attendant ministers close at hand and the wet nurse together pulled and held him back; he could not go out. He sighed and raged, refusing food, and cursed Empress Quan: "Your father is muddle-headed—he has ruined my great affair!
translations.idiomatic: Attendants and the wet nurse seized him and would not let him leave. He raged and refused food, cursing Empress Quan: "Your father is a fool—he has ruined everything!

sentences.zh: 」又遣呼紀，紀曰：「臣父奉詔不謹，負上，無面目復見。

translations.literal: " He again sent to summon Ji; Ji said: "My father received the edict without care and failed his sovereign—I have no face to see him again.
translations.idiomatic: He sent again for Quan Ji. Ji said, "My father received the edict without due care and failed his sovereign. I have no face left to appear before you.

sentences.zh: 」因自殺。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Then he killed himself.

sentences.zh: 綝使光祿勳孟宗告太廟，廢吳主為會稽王。

translations.literal: Chen sent Director of the Imperial Household Meng Zong to announce at the ancestral temple and deposed the ruler of Wu as King of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chen sent Director of the Imperial Household Meng Zong to announce at the ancestral temple and deposed the emperor as King of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 召群臣議曰：「少帝荒病昏亂，不可以處大位，承宗廟，已告先帝廢之。

translations.literal: He summoned the ministers to deliberate, saying: "The young emperor is wild, sick, and muddled; he cannot occupy the great throne or inherit the ancestral temple—I have already announced to the Former Emperor that he is deposed.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the ministers and said, "The young emperor is mad, sick, and muddled. He cannot occupy the throne or inherit the ancestral temple. I have already announced to the Former Emperor that he is deposed.

sentences.zh: 諸君若有不同者，下異議。

translations.literal: If any among you gentlemen differ, speak your dissent below.
translations.idiomatic: If any among you disagree, speak your dissent now.

sentences.zh: 」皆震怖，曰：「唯將軍令！

translations.literal: " All were terrified and said: "Only the general's command!
translations.idiomatic: All were terrified and said, "We await only the general's command!

sentences.zh: 」綝遣中書郎李崇奪吳主璽綬，以吳主罪班告遠近。

translations.literal: " Chen sent Secretariat Attendant Li Chong to seize the ruler of Wu's seal and cord, and published the ruler of Wu's crimes throughout near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chen sent Secretariat Attendant Li Chong to seize the emperor's seal and cord and published his crimes throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 尚書桓彝不肯署名，綝怒，殺之。

translations.literal: Minister of the Secretariat Huan Yi refused to sign his name; Chen was enraged and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Secretariat Huan Yi refused to sign; Sun Chen, enraged, had him killed.

sentences.zh: 典國施正勸絲林迎立琅邪王休，綝從之。

translations.literal: Director of Ceremonial Affairs Shi Zheng urged Sun Chen to welcome and establish Langya Wang Xiu; Chen followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Ceremonial Affairs Shi Zheng urged Sun Chen to welcome Langya Wang Xiu and establish him as emperor; Chen agreed.

sentences.zh: 己未，綝使宗正楷與中書郎董朝迎琅邪王於會稽。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, Chen sent Director of the Imperial Clan Kai and Secretariat Attendant Dong Chao to welcome Langya Wang from Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiwei, Sun Chen sent Director of the Imperial Clan Sun Kai and Secretariat Attendant Dong Chao to welcome Langya Wang from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 遣將軍孫耽送會稽王亮之國，亮時年十六。

translations.literal: He dispatched General Sun Dan to escort the King of Kuaiji to his fief; Liang was then sixteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched General Sun Dan to escort the deposed emperor, Sun Liang, to his fief; Liang was then sixteen.

sentences.zh: 徙全尚於零陵，尋追殺之，遷全公主於豫章。

translations.literal: Quan Shang was moved to Lingling; soon he was pursued and killed; Princess Quan was transferred to Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Shang was exiled to Lingling, then hunted down and killed; Princess Quan was moved to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊午，琅邪王行至曲阿，有老公遮王叩頭曰：「事久變生，天下喁喁，願陛下速行！

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day wuwu, as Langya Wang traveled and reached Qu'e, an old man blocked the king's path and kowtowed, saying: "Matters long delayed turn to trouble; all under Heaven murmurs—may Your Majesty hasten on!
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day wuwu, as Langya Wang traveled and reached Qu'e, an old man blocked his path and kowtowed, saying, "When matters drag on, trouble follows. The realm murmurs with unrest—may Your Majesty hurry on!

sentences.zh: 」王善之。

translations.literal: " The king thought this good.
translations.idiomatic: The king approved.

sentences.zh: 是日，進及布塞亭。

translations.literal: That day he advanced as far as Busei Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he pressed on as far as Busei Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 孫綝以琅邪王未至，欲入居富中，召百官會議，皆惶怖失色，徒唯唯而已。

translations.literal: Sun Chen, because Langya Wang had not yet arrived, wished to enter and dwell in the palace; he summoned the hundred officials to council—all were terrified and turned pale, and could only murmur assent.
translations.idiomatic: Because Langya Wang had not yet arrived, Sun Chen wished to enter the palace and take up residence there. He summoned the officials to council; all were terrified and could only murmur assent.

sentences.zh: 選曹郎虞汜曰：「明公為國伊、周，處將相之任，擅廢立之威，將上安宗廟，下惠百姓，大小踴躍，自以伊、霍復見。

translations.literal: Selection Bureau Attendant Yu Si said: "My lord, for the state, is Yi and Zhou; you occupy the rank of general and minister and wield the authority to depose and establish; you will secure the ancestral temple above and benefit the hundred clans below—great and small leap for joy, each thinking Yi and Huo have appeared again.
translations.idiomatic: Selection Bureau Attendant Yu Si said, "My lord serves the state as Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. You hold the rank of general and minister and wield the power to depose and establish rulers. You will secure the ancestral temple above and benefit the people below. Great and small rejoice, each thinking Yi Yin and Huo Guang have returned to the age.

sentences.zh: 今迎王未至而始入宮，如是，群下搖蕩，眾聽疑惑，非所以永終忠孝，揚名後世也。

translations.literal: Now you welcome the king, yet before he arrives you wish to enter the palace—if so, those below will waver and the multitude's hearing will be doubtful; this is not the way to end in lasting loyalty and filial piety, or to spread one's name in later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you wish to enter the palace before the new emperor arrives. If you do, your followers will waver and the realm will be filled with doubt. That is not the way to preserve lasting loyalty and filial piety, or to leave a noble name to posterity.

sentences.zh: 」綝不懌而止。

translations.literal: " Chen was displeased and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chen, displeased, desisted.

sentences.zh: 汜，翻之子也。

translations.literal: Si was the son of Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Si was the son of Yu Fan.

sentences.zh: 綝命弟恩行丞相事，率百僚以乘輿法駕迎琅邪王於永昌亭。

translations.literal: Chen ordered his younger brother En to act as Chancellor, leading the hundred officials with the imperial carriage and full regalia to welcome Langya Wang at Yongchang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chen ordered his younger brother En to act as Chancellor and lead the hundred officials with the imperial carriage and full regalia to welcome Langya Wang at Yongchang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 築宮，以武帳為便殿，設御坐。

translations.literal: A palace was built; the military tent served as the temporary hall, and the imperial seat was set out.
translations.idiomatic: A residence was prepared; a military tent served as the temporary hall, and the imperial seat was set in place.

sentences.zh: 己卯，王至便殿，止東廂。

translations.literal: On the day jimao the king arrived at the temporary hall and lodged in the east wing.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jimao the king arrived at the temporary hall and lodged in the east wing.

sentences.zh: 孫恩奉上璽符，王三讓，乃受。

translations.literal: Sun En presented the imperial seal and tally; the king declined three times, then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En presented the imperial seal and tally; the king declined three times, then accepted.

sentences.zh: 群臣以次奉引，王就乘輿，百官陪位。

translations.literal: The ministers in order led and guided him; the king mounted the carriage, and the hundred officials took their places beside him.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers led him in order of rank; the king mounted the carriage, and the hundred officials took their places beside him.

sentences.zh: 綝以兵千人迎於半野，拜於道側；

translations.literal: Chen with a thousand troops welcomed him halfway across the field and bowed at the roadside;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chen, with a thousand troops, met him halfway and bowed at the roadside;

sentences.zh: 王下車答拜。

translations.literal: the king descended from the carriage and returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: the king descended from the carriage and returned the bow.

sentences.zh: 即日，御正殿，大赦，改元永安。

translations.literal: That same day he ascended the main hall, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he ascended the main hall, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 孫綝稱「草莽臣」，詣闕上書，上印綬、節鉞，求避賢路。

translations.literal: Sun Chen styled himself "minister of the wilds," came to the gate and submitted a memorial, surrendered his seal and cord and battle-axe, and sought to withdraw from the path of the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chen styled himself "a humble minister of the wilds," came to the palace gate and submitted a memorial, surrendered his seal, cord, and battle-axe, and asked to yield the path to worthier men.

sentences.zh: 吳主引見慰諭，下詔以綝為丞相、荊州牧，增邑五縣；

translations.literal: The ruler of Wu summoned him for an audience, comforted and instructed him, and issued an edict appointing Chen Chancellor and Governor of Jing Province, increasing his fief by five counties;
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor received him in audience, comforted him, and issued an edict appointing Sun Chen Chancellor and Governor of Jing Province, increasing his fief by five counties;

sentences.zh: 以恩為御史大夫、衛將軍、中軍督，封縣侯。

translations.literal: En was made Censor-in-Chief, Guard General, and Area Commander of the Central Army, and enfeoffed as a district marquis.
translations.idiomatic: En was made Censor-in-Chief, Guard General, and Area Commander of the Central Army, and enfeoffed as a district marquis.

sentences.zh: 孫據、干、闓皆拜將軍，封侯。

translations.literal: Sun Ju, Gan, and Kai were all appointed generals and enfeoffed as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ju, Gan, and Kai were all appointed generals and enfeoffed as marquises.

sentences.zh: 又以長水校尉張布為輔義將軍，封永康侯。

translations.literal: Changshui Colonel Zhang Bu was also made Assistant General Who Supports Righteousness and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel of the Changshui Regiment Zhang Bu was also made Assistant General Who Supports Righteousness and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 先是，丹楊太守李衡數以事侵琅邪王，其妻習氏諫之，衡不聽。

translations.literal: Before this, Danyang Administrator Li Heng repeatedly on account of affairs encroached upon Langya Wang; his wife, the Xi clan, remonstrated with him, but Heng would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Danyang Administrator Li Heng had repeatedly wronged Langya Wang over various matters. His wife, Lady Xi, remonstrated with him, but Heng would not listen.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王上書乞徙他郡，詔徙會稽。

translations.literal: Langya Wang submitted a memorial begging to be moved to another commandery; an edict moved him to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Langya Wang submitted a memorial asking to be transferred to another commandery, and an edict moved him to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 及琅邪王即位，李衡憂懼，謂妻曰：「不用卿言，以至於此。

translations.literal: When Langya Wang ascended the throne, Li Heng was worried and afraid; he said to his wife: "I did not heed your words, and so have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: When Langya Wang ascended the throne, Li Heng was filled with dread. He said to his wife, "I did not heed your counsel, and so have come to this.

sentences.zh: 吾欲奔魏，何如？

translations.literal: I wish to flee to Wei—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: I mean to flee to Wei. What do you think?

sentences.zh: 」妻曰：「不可。

translations.literal: " The wife said: "It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: His wife replied, "You must not.

sentences.zh: 君本庶民耳，先帝相拔過重，既數作無禮，而復逆自猜嫌，逃叛求活，以此北歸，何面目見中國人乎！

translations.literal: You, lord, were originally but a commoner. The late emperor selected and elevated you far beyond your station. Already having repeatedly acted without propriety, and moreover perversely harboring suspicion in yourself, fleeing in rebellion to seek life—on this basis returning north, with what face can you meet the people of the Central Kingdom!
translations.idiomatic: You were originally nothing but a commoner. The late emperor favored and elevated you far beyond your station. You have repeatedly acted without propriety, and now perversely let suspicion fill your heart—you would flee in rebellion to save your life! If you went north on that basis, with what face could you look upon the people of the Central Kingdom!

sentences.zh: 」衡曰：「計何所出？

translations.literal: " Heng said: "From where does this plan come?
translations.idiomatic: Heng asked, "What plan do you have in mind?

sentences.zh: 」妻曰：「琅邪王素好善慕名，方欲自顯於天下，終不以私嫌殺君明矣。

translations.literal: " The wife said: "Langya Wang has always loved goodness and sought reputation. He is just now trying to show himself to the world—clearly he will never kill you over a private grudge.
translations.idiomatic: His wife replied, "Langya Wang has always loved virtue and sought fame. He wishes to distinguish himself before the world, and it is plain he will never kill you over a private resentment.

sentences.zh: 可自囚詣獄，表列前失，顯求受罪。

translations.literal: You may bind yourself and go to prison, set forth in a memorial your past faults, and openly request punishment.
translations.idiomatic: You should surrender yourself to prison, list your past offenses in a memorial, and openly ask to receive punishment.

sentences.zh: 如此，乃當逆見優饒，非但直活而已。

translations.literal: If you do this, you will in reverse meet with generous favor—not merely escape with your life.
translations.idiomatic: If you do this, he will in turn treat you with unexpected clemency—you will do more than merely save your life.

sentences.zh: 」衡從之。

translations.literal: " Heng followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Heng took her advice.

sentences.zh: 吳主詔曰：「丹楊太守李衡，以往事之嫌，自拘司敗。

translations.literal: The ruler of Wu issued an edict saying: "Danyang Administrator Li Heng, on account of suspicion over past affairs, has bound himself in the Office of Punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Wu issued an edict: "Danyang Administrator Li Heng, owing to suspicions over past affairs, has surrendered himself to the Office of Punishment.

sentences.zh: 夫射鉤、斬祛，在君為君，其遣衡還郡，勿令自疑。

translations.literal: In the matter of shooting the hook and cutting the sleeve—whoever is lord shall be served as lord. Let Heng be sent back to his commandery and not be allowed to doubt himself.
translations.idiomatic: As with shooting the hook and cutting the sleeve—whoever is sovereign shall be served as sovereign. He ordered that Heng be sent back to his commandery and not left to torment himself with doubt.

sentences.zh: 」又如威遠將軍，授以棨戟。

translations.literal: " He also made him General Who Displays Distant Majesty and conferred on him the ceremonial halberd.
translations.idiomatic: He also restored him as General Who Displays Distant Majesty and conferred on him the ceremonial halberd.

sentences.zh: 己丑，吳主封故南陽王和子皓為烏程侯。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, the ruler of Wu enfeoffed Sun Hao, son of the former Prince of Nanyang Sun He, as Marquis of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, the ruler of Wu enfeoffed Sun Hao, son of the former Prince of Nanyang Sun He, as Marquis of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 群臣奏立皇后、太子，吳主曰：「朕以寡德，奉承洪業，蒞事日淺，恩澤未敷，后妃之號，嗣子之位，非所急也。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers memorialized to establish an empress and crown prince. The ruler of Wu said: "I, with meager virtue, have inherited the great enterprise. My days in office have been brief and my favors not yet widely bestowed—the titles of empress and the position of heir are not matters of urgency.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers pressed to have an empress and crown prince appointed. The ruler of Wu said, "My virtue is slight and I have only lately inherited this vast enterprise. I have governed but a short while and have not yet showered my grace upon the realm—the titles of empress and heir are not what I need most urgently right now.

sentences.zh: 」有司固請，吳主不許。

translations.literal: " The responsible officials pressed their request repeatedly, but the ruler of Wu would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The officials pressed the point, but the ruler of Wu refused.

sentences.zh: 孫綝奉牛酒詣吳主，吳主不受，繼詣左將軍張布。

translations.literal: Sun Chen brought oxen and wine as gifts to the ruler of Wu; the ruler would not accept them, so Chen went next to Left General Zhang Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chen presented oxen and wine to the ruler of Wu, who declined them. Chen then went to Left General Zhang Bu.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，出怨言曰：「初廢少主時，多勸吾自為之者。

translations.literal: When the wine had gone to his head, he spoke words of resentment, saying: "When we first deposed the young ruler, many urged me to take the throne myself.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was deep in his cups, he blurted out bitter complaints: "When we first deposed the young emperor, many urged me to take the throne myself.

sentences.zh: 吾以陛下賢明，故迎之。

translations.literal: I judged Your Majesty wise and enlightened, and so I welcomed you to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: I thought Your Majesty wise and enlightened, and so I welcomed you to the throne instead.

sentences.zh: 帝非我不立，今上禮見拒，是與凡臣無異，當復改圖耳。

translations.literal: Your Majesty would not have been enthroned without me. Now you refuse me the courtesies due at an audience—I am treated no differently from any ordinary minister. I shall have to rethink my course.
translations.idiomatic: You owe your throne to me. Now you refuse me the courtesies of an audience—I am treated no better than any ordinary minister. I shall have to change my plans.

sentences.zh: 」布以告吳主，吳主銜之，恐其有變，數加賞賜。

translations.literal: " Bu reported this to the ruler of Wu, who harbored resentment but, fearing Chen might rebel, repeatedly showered him with rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Bu reported this to the ruler of Wu, who took bitter offense but, fearing Chen might turn against him, repeatedly showered him with gifts.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，吳主詔曰：「大將軍掌中外諸軍事，事統煩多，其加衛將軍、御史大夫恩侍中，與大將軍分省諸事。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, the ruler of Wu issued an edict: "The Grand General holds authority over all military affairs at home and abroad, and his duties are numerous and complex. Let Guard General and Secretary Director Sun En also be made Palace Attendant, to share with the Grand General in managing the various affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, the ruler of Wu issued an edict: "The Grand General commands all military affairs within and beyond the court, and the burden of his duties is immense. Let Guard General and Secretary Director Sun En also be made Palace Attendant, to divide administrative business with the Grand General.

sentences.zh: 」或有告綝懷怨悔上，欲圖反者，吳主執以付綝，綝殺之，由是益懼，因孟宗求出屯武昌；

translations.literal: " Some reported that Chen nursed resentment against the ruler and regretted enthroning him, and intended to rebel; the ruler of Wu seized the informers and handed them over to Chen, and Chen killed them. From this he grew still more fearful and, through Meng Zong, asked to go out and garrison Wuchang;
translations.idiomatic: Some reported that Chen harbored resentment against the emperor and regretted having raised him to the throne, and intended rebellion. The ruler of Wu had the informants arrested and delivered to Chen, who had them killed. Chen was thus all the more terrified, and through Meng Zong asked permission to garrison Wuchang;

sentences.zh: 吳主許之。

translations.literal: The ruler of Wu consented.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Wu agreed.

sentences.zh: 綝盡敕所督中營精兵萬餘人，皆令裝載，又取武庫兵器，吳主咸令給與。

translations.literal: Chen ordered all the more than ten thousand crack troops of the central camp under his command to ready their gear for transport, and also took weapons from the armory—all of which the ruler of Wu ordered be supplied to him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen mustered the more than ten thousand elite troops of the central garrison under his command and had them load for departure, and also drew weapons from the arsenal—the ruler of Wu granted him everything.

sentences.zh: 綝求中書兩郎典知荊州諸軍事，主者奏中書不應外出，吳主特聽之。

translations.literal: Chen requested two Secretariat attendants to manage military affairs in Jing Province; the responsible officials memorialized that Secretariat staff should not be sent outside the capital, but the ruler of Wu made an exception and permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Chen asked for two Secretariat clerks to oversee military affairs in Jing Province. The responsible officials replied that Secretariat staff should not be sent abroad, but the ruler of Wu made an exception for him.

sentences.zh: 其所請求，一無違者。

translations.literal: Of everything he requested, not one was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Not a single request of his was denied.

sentences.zh: 將軍魏邈說吳主曰：「綝居外，必有變。

translations.literal: General Wei Miao urged the ruler of Wu, saying: "If Chen stays outside the capital, there is bound to be trouble.
translations.idiomatic: General Wei Miao advised the ruler of Wu, "With Chen holding power outside the capital, trouble is sure to come.

sentences.zh: 」武衛士施朔又告綝謀反。

translations.literal: " Palace guard soldier Shi Shuo also reported that Chen was plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guard soldier Shi Shuo also reported that Chen intended to rebel.

sentences.zh: 吳主將討綝，密問輔義將軍張布，布曰：「左將軍丁奉，雖不能吏書，而計略過人，能斷大事。

translations.literal: The ruler of Wu was about to move against Chen and secretly consulted Auxiliary General Zhang Bu. Bu said: "Left General Ding Feng, though unable to manage written documents, surpasses others in stratagem and can decide great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Wu resolved to suppress Chen and secretly consulted Auxiliary General Zhang Bu. Bu said, "Left General Ding Feng, though he cannot manage written documents, surpasses others in strategy and can decide great affairs.

sentences.zh: 」吳主召奉告之，且問以計畫。

translations.literal: " The ruler of Wu summoned Ding Feng, told him of the plan, and asked his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Wu summoned Ding Feng, told him the plan, and asked his advice.

sentences.zh: 奉曰：「丞相兄弟支黨甚盛，恐人心不同，不可卒制；

translations.literal: Feng said: "The Chancellor and his brothers have a vast faction. I fear hearts will not be united and he cannot be taken at once;
translations.idiomatic: Ding Feng said, "The Chancellor and his brothers command an extensive faction. I fear opinions will be divided and we cannot seize him all at once;

sentences.zh: 可因臘會有陛兵以誅之。

translations.literal: We can use the year-end sacrificial feast, when the guard troops will be present, to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: We can take advantage of the winter sacrificial feast, when the palace guard will be on hand, to put him to death.

sentences.zh: 」吳主從之。

translations.literal: " The ruler of Wu followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Wu accepted the plan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁卯，建業中謠言明會有變，綝聞之，不悅。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day dingmao, rumors spread through Jianye that there would be trouble at the coming assembly; Chen heard of this and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dingmao, a rumor spread through Jianye that something would happen at the coming feast assembly; when Chen heard this, he was displeased.

sentences.zh: 夜，大風，發屋揚沙，綝益懼。

translations.literal: That night a great wind blew, tearing off roofs and whirling sand; Chen grew still more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: That night a fierce wind arose, ripping off roofs and hurling sand through the streets; Chen was all the more terrified.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，臘會，綝稱疾不至；

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, the year-end feast was held; Chen claimed illness and did not attend;
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, the year-end feast was held. Chen pleaded illness and stayed away;

sentences.zh: 吳主強起之，使者十餘輩，綝不得已，將入，眾止焉。

translations.literal: The ruler of Wu repeatedly sent messengers—more than ten rounds in all—to summon him. Chen had no choice but to go. When he was about to enter, the crowd stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Wu sent more than ten messengers in succession to force him to attend. Chen had no choice but to go. As he was about to enter, his followers barred his way.

sentences.zh: 綝曰：「國家屢有命，不可辭。

translations.literal: Chen said: "The state has repeatedly issued orders—they cannot be declined.
translations.idiomatic: Chen said, "The state has repeatedly summoned me—I cannot refuse.

sentences.zh: 可豫整兵，令府內起火，因是可得速還。

translations.literal: Prepare the troops in advance, and have a fire set inside the residence—then we can get away quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Ready the troops beforehand and set a fire inside the mansion; then we can withdraw at once.

sentences.zh: 」遂入，尋而火起，綝求出，吳主曰：「外兵自多，不足煩丞相也。

translations.literal: " He then entered; soon the fire broke out. Chen asked to leave, and the ruler of Wu said: "The troops outside are ample—there is no need to trouble the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered. Before long the fire broke out. Chen asked to leave, and the ruler of Wu said, "There are plenty of troops outside—there is no need for the Chancellor to go out.

sentences.zh: 」綝起離席，奉、布目左右縛之。

translations.literal: " Chen rose from his seat; Ding Feng and Zhang Bu signaled those at hand to bind him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen started to rise from his seat; Ding Feng and Zhang Bu signaled the men beside them to seize and bind him.

sentences.zh: 綝叩頭曰：「願徙交州。

translations.literal: Chen kowtowed and said: "I beg to be banished to Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen kowtowed and pleaded, "I beg to be exiled to Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 」吳主曰：「卿何以不徙滕胤、呂據於交州乎！

translations.literal: " The ruler of Wu said: "Why did you not banish Teng Yin and Lü Ju to Jiaozhou!
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Wu retorted, "Why did you not send Teng Yin and Lü Ju into exile in Jiaozhou!

sentences.zh: 」綝復曰：「願沒為官奴。

translations.literal: " Chen again said: "I beg to be made a government slave.
translations.idiomatic: Chen pleaded again, "Then let me be made a government slave.

sentences.zh: 」吳主曰：「卿何不以胤、據為奴乎！

translations.literal: " The ruler of Wu said: "Why did you not make Yin and Ju slaves!
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Wu said, "Why did you not make Yin and Ju slaves!

sentences.zh: 」遂斬之。

translations.literal: " He was then beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was then executed.

sentences.zh: 以綝首令其眾曰：「諸與綝同謀者，皆赦之。

translations.literal: With Chen's head he addressed Chen's followers: "All who plotted with Chen are pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Displaying Chen's head, he announced to Chen's followers, "All who joined Chen's plot are pardoned.

sentences.zh: 」放仗者五千人。

translations.literal: " Five thousand men laid down their arms.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand men laid down their weapons.

sentences.zh: 孫闓乘船欲降北，追殺之。

translations.literal: Sun Kan attempted to take ship and surrender to the north; he was pursued and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kan tried to take ship and surrender to the north; pursuers overtook and killed him.

sentences.zh: 夷綝三族，發孫峻棺，取其印綬，斫其木而埋之。

translations.literal: Chen's three clans were exterminated. Sun Jun's coffin was opened, his seal and sash taken, the wood of the coffin chopped up and buried.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's entire clan to the third degree was wiped out. Sun Jun's coffin was opened, his seal and cord were seized, and the coffin wood was hacked apart and buried.

sentences.zh: 己巳，吳主以張布為中軍督。

translations.literal: On the day jisi, the ruler of Wu made Zhang Bu Director of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, the ruler of Wu appointed Zhang Bu Director of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 改葬諸葛恪、滕胤、呂據等，其罹恪等事遠徒者，一切召還。

translations.literal: Zhuge Ke, Teng Yin, Lü Ju, and the like were reburied with honor; those who had been exiled far off on account of Ke and the others were all recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke, Teng Yin, Lü Ju, and others were given proper reburials, and all who had been exiled on account of Ke and his associates were summoned home.

sentences.zh: 朝臣有乞為諸葛恪立碑者，吳主詔曰：「盛夏出軍，士卒傷損，無尺寸之功，不可謂能；

translations.literal: Some court ministers asked that a stele be erected for Zhuge Ke. The ruler of Wu issued an edict: "He led troops out in the height of summer, and the soldiers suffered injury and loss without the slightest measure of merit—that cannot be called capable;
translations.idiomatic: When court ministers asked to erect a monument for Zhuge Ke, the ruler of Wu replied, "He marched out troops in the height of summer. Soldiers were wounded and killed, yet he won not the slightest glory—that cannot be called competence;

sentences.zh: 受托孤之任，死於豎子之手，不可謂智。

translations.literal: Entrusted with the charge of supporting the orphan emperor, he died at the hands of a petty ruffian—that cannot be called wise.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted with the guardianship of the orphan emperor, he died at the hands of a common bully—that cannot be called wisdom.

sentences.zh: 」遂寢。

translations.literal: " The proposal was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 初，漢昭烈留魏延鎮漢中，皆實兵諸圍以御外敵，敵若來攻，使不得入。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Han's Emperor Zhaolie left Wei Yan to guard Hanzhong, strong garrisons were placed at the various encirclement forts to resist external enemies—if the enemy came to attack, they were kept from entering.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Zhaolie of Han left Wei Yan to guard Hanzhong, he manned the surrounding forts with real troops to hold off invaders; should the enemy attack, they were prevented from breaking in.

sentences.zh: 及興勢之役，王平捍拒曹爽，皆承此制。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Xingshi, when Wang Ping defended against Cao Shuang, he followed this same arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Xingshi, when Wang Ping held off Cao Shuang, he followed this same system.

sentences.zh: 及姜維用事，建議以為「錯守諸圍，適可禦敵，不獲大利。

translations.literal: After Jiang Wei came into power, he proposed his view that "dispersed defense of the various forts can merely repel the enemy and wins no great gain.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiang Wei took control, he argued that "scattering troops among the surrounding forts can only ward off the enemy; it brings no great advantage.

sentences.zh: 不若使聞敵至，諸圍皆斂兵聚谷，退就漢、樂二城，聽敵入平，重關頭鎮守以捍之，令遊軍旁出以伺其虛。

translations.literal: It would be better, when word comes that the enemy is approaching, to have every fort gather its troops and grain and withdraw to the twin strongholds of Han and Le, allowing the enemy to advance onto the plain while heavy forces guard the barrier passes and hold them off, and mobile units strike out on the flanks to watch for openings.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to wait until the enemy is reported near, then have every fort pull in its troops and grain and fall back on the two cities of Han and Le. Let the enemy onto the plain while strong garrisons hold the barrier passes, and dispatch raiding columns to strike where the enemy is weak.

sentences.zh: 敵攻關不克，野無散谷，千里運糧，自然疲乏；

translations.literal: If the enemy assaults the passes without success and finds no grain scattered in the countryside, they must transport provisions a thousand li—naturally they grow exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy fails to take the passes and finds no grain in the fields, they must haul supplies a thousand li—they will naturally wear themselves out;

sentences.zh: 引退之日，然後諸城並出，與遊軍並力搏之，此殄敵之術也。

translations.literal: On the day they retreat, then all the cities sally forth together and, with the mobile units, join forces to strike them—this is the method for destroying the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: and on the day they withdraw, every stronghold can sally forth together while the raiding columns join in the assault—this is the way to annihilate an invader.

sentences.zh: 」於是漢主令督漢中胡濟卻住漢壽，監軍王含守樂城，護軍蔣斌守漢城。

translations.literal: " The ruler of Han thereupon ordered Supervisor of Hanzhong Hu Ji to withdraw and hold Hanshou, Supervisor of the Army Wang Han to guard Lecheng, and Protector of the Army Jiang Bin to guard Hancheng.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Han accordingly ordered Supervisor of Hanzhong Hu Ji to fall back and hold Hanshou, Army Supervisor Wang Han to defend Lecheng, and Protector of the Army Jiang Bin to defend Hancheng.

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公下甘露四年（

translations.literal: Under the Duke of Gaoguixiang, fourth year of Ganlu (
translations.idiomatic: Under the Duke of Gaoguixiang, fourth year of Ganlu (

sentences.zh: 己卯，公元二五九年）

translations.literal: jimao, AD 259)
translations.idiomatic: the year jimao, AD 259)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，黃龍二見寧陵井中。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, a pair of yellow dragons appeared in a well at Ningling.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, a pair of yellow dragons appeared in a well at Ningling.

sentences.zh: 先是，頓丘、冠軍、陽夏進中屢有龍見，群臣以為吉祥，帝曰：「龍者，君德也，上不在天，下不在田，而數屈於井，非嘉兆也。

translations.literal: Earlier, at Dunqiu, Guanjun, Yangxia, and Jinying, dragons had repeatedly appeared. The ministers took this as auspicious, but the emperor said: "The dragon embodies a ruler's virtue. It belongs neither above in Heaven nor below in the fields, yet time and again it is confined to a well—this is no lucky sign.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, at Dunqiu, Guanjun, Yangxia, and Jinying, dragons had appeared again and again. The ministers hailed these as good omens, but the emperor said, "The dragon embodies the virtue of a ruler. It should belong neither above in Heaven nor below in the fields, yet repeatedly it is trapped in wells—this is no happy sign.

sentences.zh: 」作《潛龍詩》以自諷，司馬昭見而惡之。

translations.literal: " He composed the "Poem of the Hidden Dragon" to admonish himself, and Sima Zhao saw it and hated him for it.
translations.idiomatic: He composed the "Poem of the Hidden Dragon" as a self-admonition, and when Sima Zhao read it, he took offense.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，京陵穆侯王昶卒。

translations.literal: In summer, the sixth month, Wang Chang, Marquis of Jingling, died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the sixth month, Wang Chang, Marquis of Jingling, died.

sentences.zh: 漢主封其子諶為北地王，恂為新興王，虔為上黨王。

translations.literal: The ruler of Han enfeoffed his son Liu Chen as Prince of Beidi, Liu Xun as Prince of Xinxing, and Liu Qian as Prince of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Han enfeoffed his sons Liu Chen as Prince of Beidi, Liu Xun as Prince of Xinxing, and Liu Qian as Prince of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 尚書令陳祗以巧佞有寵於漢主，姜維雖位在祗上，而多率眾在外，希親朝政，權任不及祗。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Chen Zhi, through ingratiating cleverness, had won the ruler of Han's favor. Though Jiang Wei's rank was above Zhi's, he spent much of his time leading troops abroad and rarely attended to court affairs, so his authority and responsibilities did not match Zhi's.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Chen Zhi won the ruler of Han's favor through flattering cleverness. Although Jiang Wei outranked him, Wei spent most of his time leading armies in the field and seldom came near court politics, and so his power and trust did not equal Zhi's.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，丙子，祗卒；

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on bingzi, Zhi died;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the eighth month, on bingzi, Zhi died;

sentences.zh: 漢主以僕射義陽董厥為尚書令，尚書諸葛瞻為僕射。

translations.literal: The ruler of Han appointed Dong Jue of Yiyang, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, as Director of the Masters of Writing, and Director of the Masters of Writing Zhuge Zhan as Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Han made Vice Director Dong Jue of Yiyang Director of the Masters of Writing, and Director Zhuge Zhan Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，車騎將軍孫壹為婢所殺。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, Sun Yi, General of Chariots and Cavalry, was killed by a maid servant.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the eleventh month, Sun Yi, General of Chariots and Cavalry, was killed by a maidservant.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以王基為征南將軍，都督荊州諸軍事。

translations.literal: This year, Wang Ji was made General Who Campaigns to the South and given overall command of military affairs in Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Wang Ji was appointed General Who Campaigns to the South and put in overall command of military affairs in Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 元皇帝上

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan, Part One

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公下景元元年（

translations.literal: Under the Duke of Gaoguixiang, first year of Jingyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Under the Duke of Gaoguixiang, first year of Jingyuan (

sentences.zh: 庚辰，公元二六零年）

translations.literal: gengchen, AD 260)
translations.idiomatic: the year gengchen, AD 260)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the first day, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on the new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，詔有司率遵前命，復進大將軍昭位相國，封晉公，加九錫。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, an edict ordered the responsible officials strictly to follow the previous command and again advance Grand General Zhao to Chancellor of State, enfeoff him as Duke of Jin, and grant him the nine bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, an edict ordered the responsible officials to follow the previous command without delay and again promote Grand General Zhao to Chancellor of State, enfeoff him as Duke of Jin, and grant him the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 帝見威權日去，不勝其忿。

translations.literal: The emperor saw his authority daily ebbing away and could not contain his rage.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor watched his authority slip away day by day and could not contain his fury.

sentences.zh: 五月，己丑，召侍中王沈、尚書王經、散騎常侍王業，謂曰：「司馬昭之心，路人所知也。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day jichou, he summoned Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Shen, Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jing, and Regular Attendant Wang Ye, and said: "Sima Zhao's intentions are known even to passersby on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jichou, he summoned Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Shen, Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jing, and Regular Attendant Wang Ye, and said, "Sima Zhao's ambitions are plain to every man in the street.

sentences.zh: 吾不能坐受廢辱，今日當與卿自出討之。

translations.literal: I cannot sit and accept disgrace and deposition. Today I shall go out with you to strike at him.
translations.idiomatic: I will not sit still and accept humiliation and deposition. Today I shall ride out with you to attack him.

sentences.zh: 」王經曰：「昔魯昭公不忍季氏，敗走失國，為天下笑。

translations.literal: " Wang Jing said: "In antiquity Duke Zhao of Lu could not endure the Ji clan and fled in defeat, losing his state, becoming the laughter of the world.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing said, "Long ago Duke Zhao of Lu could not tolerate the Ji clan. He was defeated, fled, and lost his state, and became a laughingstock to the world.

sentences.zh: 今權在其門，為日久矣。

translations.literal: Now power lies in their household and has for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Today power rests in the Sima house and has done so for a long time.

sentences.zh: 朝廷四方皆為之致死，不顧逆順之理，非一日也。

translations.literal: From all quarters of the court men will die for them, heedless of whether that is right or wrong—not for a single day only.
translations.idiomatic: Men throughout the court and the empire will die for them without reckoning right or wrong—and this has been so for more than a day.

sentences.zh: 且宿衛空闕，兵甲寡弱，陛下何所資用；

translations.literal: Moreover the palace guard is empty and the armor few—what resources has Your Majesty to rely upon;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the imperial guard is understrength and arms are few—what force does Your Majesty have to rely on;

sentences.zh: 而一旦如此，無乃欲除疾而更深之邪！

translations.literal: Yet to act so suddenly—are you not seeking to cure a disease only to plunge the blade deeper!
translations.idiomatic: and to act on a sudden impulse like this—is it not like trying to cure an illness and driving the knife in deeper!

sentences.zh: 禍殆不測，宜見重詳。

translations.literal: The danger is incalculable. Your Majesty should give this further careful thought.
translations.idiomatic: The peril is beyond reckoning. Your Majesty ought to reconsider at length.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃出懷中黃素詔投地曰：「行之決矣！

translations.literal: " The emperor then produced the yellow-silk edict from his bosom, cast it to the ground, and said: "My mind is made up!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then drew the yellow silk edict from his robe, flung it to the ground, and cried, "I have made up my mind!

sentences.zh: 正使死何懼，況不必死邪！

translations.literal: Even if I must die, what is there to fear—and why should I not also live!
translations.idiomatic: Let me die if I must—what is there to fear? I may not die at all!

sentences.zh: 」於是入白太后。

translations.literal: " He then went in to report to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He then went in to inform the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 沈、業奔走告昭，呼經欲與俱，經不從。

translations.literal: Wang Shen and Wang Ye ran to tell Zhao, calling for Wang Jing to come with them; Jing would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen and Wang Ye rushed off to warn Zhao and called for Wang Jing to come with them; Jing refused.

sentences.zh: 帝遂拔劍升輦，率殿中宿衛蒼頭官僮鼓噪而出。

translations.literal: The emperor then drew his sword, mounted the carriage, and led out the palace guards, personal attendants, and eunuch servants, shouting as they went.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drew his sword, mounted his carriage, and led out the palace guards, personal attendants, and eunuchs, shouting as they marched.

sentences.zh: 昭弟屯騎校尉人由遇帝於東止車門，左右呵之，人由眾奔走。

translations.literal: Zhao's younger brother Ren You, Colonel of the Cavalry Guard for the Retinue, met the emperor at the East Halting Gate. Those at the emperor's side shouted at him, and Ren You fled through the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's younger brother Ren You, Colonel of the Cavalry Guard for the Retinue, met the emperor at the East Halting Gate. The emperor's escort shouted him down, and Ren You fled pell-mell through the crowd.

sentences.zh: 中護軍賈充自外入，逆與帝戰於南闕下，帝自用劍。

translations.literal: Central Protector of the Army Jia Chong came in from outside and confronted the emperor in battle beneath the southern gate; the emperor himself wielded his sword.
translations.idiomatic: Central Protector of the Army Jia Chong came in from outside and met the emperor in combat beneath the southern gate; the emperor fought with his own sword.

sentences.zh: 眾欲退，騎督成人卒弟太子舍人濟問充曰：「事急矣，當雲何？

translations.literal: The troops were about to retreat when Cavalry Supervisor Cheng Ji's younger brother, Crown Prince's Attendant Ji, asked Chong: "The crisis is upon us—what are we to do?
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers were about to fall back when Ji, younger brother of Cavalry Supervisor Cheng Ji and an attache of the heir apparent, asked Chong, "Matters are desperate—what shall we do?

sentences.zh: 」充曰；

translations.literal: " Chong said;
translations.idiomatic: Chong replied;

sentences.zh: 「司馬公畜養汝等，正為今日。

translations.literal: "The Duke of Sima raised and kept you precisely for this day.
translations.idiomatic: "The Duke of Sima has kept and fed you for this very day.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，無所問也！

translations.literal: Today's affair brooks no questioning!
translations.idiomatic: Today's affair permits no hesitation!

sentences.zh: 」濟即抽戈前刺帝，殞於車下。

translations.literal: " Ji at once drew his halberd and thrust forward, stabbing the emperor, who fell dead beneath the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Ji immediately drew his spear and ran the emperor through; the emperor fell dead beside the carriage.

sentences.zh: 昭聞之，大驚，自投於地。

translations.literal: When Zhao heard of this, he was greatly alarmed and threw himself to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao heard the news, he was stricken with alarm and threw himself to the ground.

sentences.zh: 太傅孚奔往，枕帝股而哭，甚哀，曰；

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Fu rushed up, laid his head on the emperor's thigh, and wept bitterly, saying;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Fu rushed forward, pillowed his head on the emperor's thigh, and wept in anguish, saying;

sentences.zh: 「殺陛下者，臣之罪也！

translations.literal: "To have killed Your Majesty is my crime!
translations.idiomatic: "The killing of Your Majesty is my fault!

sentences.zh: 昭入殿中，召群臣會議。

translations.literal: Zhao entered the hall and summoned the assembled ministers to confer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao entered the palace hall and convened the ministers for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射陳泰不至，昭使其舅尚書荀顗召之，泰曰：「世之論者以泰方於舅，今舅不如泰也。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Chen Tai did not come. Zhao sent his maternal uncle, Master of Writing Xun Yi, to summon him. Tai said: "Those who discuss affairs in the world compare Tai with his uncle; now the uncle is not Tai's equal."
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Chen Tai did not appear. Zhao sent his maternal uncle, Master of Writing Xun Yi, to fetch him. Tai said, "People who talk about such things compare me with my uncle—and now my uncle is not my equal."

sentences.zh: 」子弟內外鹹共逼之，乃入，見昭，悲慟。

translations.literal: " Relatives young and old, inside and outside, all together pressed him; he then entered, saw Zhao, and grieved bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives young and old, near and far, all pressed him together; at last he went in, saw Zhao, and wept in anguish.

sentences.zh: 昭亦對之泣曰：「玄伯，卿何以處我？

translations.literal: Zhao also wept in reply and said: "Xuanbo, how would you have me deal with this?
translations.idiomatic: Zhao wept in turn and said, "Xuanbo, what am I to do?

sentences.zh: 」泰曰：「獨有斬賈充，少可以謝天下耳。

translations.literal: " Tai said: "There is only beheading Jia Chong— that alone might slightly appease the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Tai said, "There is only one course: execute Jia Chong. That alone might begin to satisfy the realm."

sentences.zh: 」昭久之曰：「卿更思其次。

translations.literal: " After a long while Zhao said: "Think again for a lesser measure."
translations.idiomatic: After a long silence Zhao said, "Think of some lesser remedy."

sentences.zh: 」泰曰：「泰言惟有進於此，不知其次。

translations.literal: " Tai said: "What I have said can only go further than this; I know no lesser course."
translations.idiomatic: Tai said, "What I have proposed can only be taken further, not reduced. I know no lesser course."

sentences.zh: 」昭乃不復更言。

translations.literal: " Zhao then spoke no further on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said nothing more.

sentences.zh: 顗，彧之子也。

translations.literal: Yi was the son of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was the son of Xun Yu.

sentences.zh: 太后下令，罪狀高貴鄉公，廢為庶人，葬以民禮。

translations.literal: The empress dowager issued an edict listing the offenses of the Duke of Gaoguixiang, deposed him as a commoner, and ordered burial according to commoners' rites.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager issued an edict enumerating the Duke of Gaoguixiang's crimes, deposed him to commoner status, and ordered him buried with the rites due a private citizen.

sentences.zh: 收王經及其家屬付廷尉。

translations.literal: Wang Jing and his family members were seized and delivered to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing and his household were arrested and handed over to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 經謝其母，母顏色不變，笑而應曰：「人誰不死，正恐不得其所」以此並命，何恨之有！

translations.literal: Jing took leave of his mother. Her countenance did not change; smiling she replied: "Who among men does not die? I only fear not dying in the proper place." To die together in this way— what regret could there be!
translations.idiomatic: Jing bade farewell to his mother. Her face did not change; smiling, she answered, "Who does not die? I only fear dying in the wrong way." To die together like this— what is there to regret!

sentences.zh: 」及就誅，故吏向雄哭，哀動一市。

translations.literal: " When the execution came, his former subordinate Xiang Xiong wept; the grief moved the whole market.
translations.idiomatic: When the execution was carried out, his former subordinate Xiang Xiong wept so bitterly that the whole marketplace was shaken with grief.

sentences.zh: 王沈以功封安平侯。

translations.literal: Wang Shen was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anping for his service.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anping for his part in the affair.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，太傅孚等上言，請以王禮葬高貴鄉公，太后許之。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, Grand Tutor Fu and others submitted a memorial requesting that the Duke of Gaoguixiang be buried with princely rites; the empress dowager granted it.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day, Grand Tutor Fu and others memorialized the throne asking that the Duke of Gaoguixiang be buried with princely honors; the empress dowager consented.

sentences.zh: 使中護軍司馬炎迎燕王宇之子常道鄉公璜於鄴，以為明帝嗣。

translations.literal: He sent Central Protector of the Army Sima Yan to welcome Changdao Township Duke Huang, son of Prince of Yan Cao Yu, from Ye, to serve as heir to Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Central Protector of the Army Sima Yan to Ye to bring back Changdao Township Duke Huang, son of Prince of Yan Cao Yu, as the successor to Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 炎，昭之子也。

translations.literal: Yan was Zhao's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was Zhao's son.

sentences.zh: 辛卿，群公奏太后自今令書皆稱詔制。

translations.literal: On the day xinqing, the assembled ministers memorialized the empress dowager that from now on her orders and documents should all be styled edicts and statutes.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinqing day, the assembled ministers memorialized the empress dowager that henceforth her orders and written instructions should all be styled edicts and statutes.

sentences.zh: 癸卿，司馬昭固讓相國、晉公、九錫之命，太后詔許之。

translations.literal: On the day guiqing, Sima Zhao firmly declined the appointments as Chancellor, Duke of Jin, and the Nine Bestowals; the empress dowager issued an edict granting his request.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiqing day, Sima Zhao firmly declined the appointments as Chancellor, Duke of Jin, and bearer of the Nine Bestowals; the empress dowager issued an edict accepting his refusal.

sentences.zh: 戊申，昭上言：「成濟兄弟大逆不道。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, Zhao submitted a memorial: "The brothers Cheng Ji have committed the greatest treason."
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day, Zhao submitted a memorial stating that the brothers Cheng Ji had committed the gravest treason.

sentences.zh: 」夷其族。

translations.literal: " Their clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Their entire clan was exterminated.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸丑，太后詔常道鄉公更名奐。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day guichou: the empress dowager decreed that Changdao Township Duke should change his name to Huan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the guichou day, the empress dowager decreed that Changdao Township Duke should take the name Huan.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，常道鄉公入洛陽，是日，即皇帝位，年十五，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, Changdao Township Duke entered Luoyang. That same day he ascended the imperial throne. He was fifteen years old. A general amnesty was declared and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day, Changdao Township Duke entered Luoyang; that same day he took the throne. He was fifteen. A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，詔進司馬昭爵位九錫如前，昭固讓，乃止。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, an edict advanced Sima Zhao's rank, enfeoffment, and Nine Bestowals as before; Zhao firmly declined, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day, an edict again offered Sima Zhao advancement in rank, enfeoffment, and the Nine Bestowals as before; Zhao firmly declined, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以尚書左僕射王觀為司空。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Guan was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Guan was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 吳都尉嚴密建議作浦裡塘，群臣皆以為難；

translations.literal: Wu Commandant Yan Mi proposed building the Puli Pond embankment; all the ministers regarded it as difficult;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Commandant Yan Mi proposed building the Puli embankment pond; all the ministers considered the project impracticable;

sentences.zh: 唯衛將軍陳留濮陽興以為可成，遂會諸軍民就作，功費不可勝數，士卒多死亡，民大愁怨。

translations.literal: Only Defender-in-Chief Pu Yangxing of Chenliu held that it could be completed. Thereupon troops and commoners were all assembled for the work. Labor and expense could not be counted; many soldiers died, and the people were greatly aggrieved and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Only Defender-in-Chief Yang Xing of Puyang in Chenliu thought it could be done. Troops and civilians were massed for the labor; the cost in effort and treasure was beyond reckoning, many soldiers died, and the people were deeply embittered.

sentences.zh: 會稽郡謠言王亮當還為天子，而亮宮人告亮使巫禱祠，有惡言，有司以聞。

translations.literal: In Kuaiji commandery a song said Wang Liang would return to become emperor. Palace women of Liang reported that Liang had sent wizards to pray and offer sacrifices, with malign words. The authorities reported this.
translations.idiomatic: In Kuaiji commandery a ballad spread saying Wang Liang would return to become emperor. Meanwhile, women of Liang's household reported that he had employed shamans to pray and sacrifice with seditious words; the authorities reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 吳主黜亮為候官侯，遣之國；

translations.literal: The ruler of Wu demoted Liang to Marquis of Houguan and sent him to his fief;
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Wu degraded Liang to Marquis of Houguan and sent him away to his fief;

sentences.zh: 亮自殺，衛送者皆伏罪。

translations.literal: Liang killed himself; those who escorted him were all punished for their crime.
translations.idiomatic: Liang killed himself, and those who had guarded and escorted him were all punished.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，陽鄉肅侯王觀卒。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Wang Guan, Marquis Su of Yangxiang, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, Wang Guan, Marquis Su of Yangxiang, died.

sentences.zh: 十一月，詔尊燕王，待以殊禮。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: an edict honored the Prince of Yan and treated him with special rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, an edict elevated the Prince of Yan and accorded him exceptional honors.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲午，以司隸校尉王祥為司空。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day jiawu: Director of the Masters of Writing for the Capital Region Wang Xiang was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the jiawu day, Director of the Masters of Writing for the Capital Region Wang Xiang was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 尚書王沈為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Master of Writing Wang Shen was appointed Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Wang Shen was appointed Inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 初到，下教敕屬城及士民曰：「若有能陳長吏可否，說百姓所患者，給谷五百斛。

translations.literal: When he first arrived, he issued an instruction to the subordinate prefectures and the gentry and commoners, saying: "If anyone can state whether the chief officials are fit or unfit, or report the people's grievances, five hundred hu of grain will be given."
translations.idiomatic: When he first took up his post, he issued an instruction to the subordinate commanderies and to gentry and commoners alike: "Anyone who can report whether local officials are fit for office, or describe the people's hardships, will receive five hundred hu of grain."

sentences.zh: 若說刺史得失、朝政寬猛者，給谷千斛。

translations.literal: If anyone speaks of the inspector's strengths and faults, or whether court governance is lenient or severe, one thousand hu of grain will be given.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who speaks of the inspector's merits and failings, or of whether court policy is too lenient or too harsh, will receive one thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 」主簿陳廞、褚□入白曰：「教旨思聞苦言，示以勸賞。

translations.literal: " Chief Clerks Chen Yin and Chu □ entered to report, saying: "The instruction's intent is to desire to hear bitter words and to display reward as encouragement."
translations.idiomatic: His chief clerks Chen Yin and Chu Lüe came in to report, "Your instruction shows that you wish to hear plain, unwelcome counsel and that you mean to encourage it with rewards."

sentences.zh: 竊恐拘介之士或憚賞而不言，貪昧之人將慕利而妄舉。

translations.literal: We privately fear that stiff and principled gentlemen may dread the reward and not speak, while greedy and benighted men will seek profit and recklessly bring accusations.
translations.idiomatic: We fear that principled men may keep silent for fear of seeming to chase a prize, while the greedy and corrupt will invent charges to win the grain.

sentences.zh: 苛不合宜，賞不虛行，則遠聽者未知當否之所在，徒見言之不用，謂設而不行。

translations.literal: If the strictures are inappropriate and rewards are not genuinely conferred, then distant listeners will not know where right and wrong lie; they will merely see that words are not acted upon and conclude the offer was made but not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: If the standards are unsuitable and rewards are not truly paid out, those far away will not know what is right or wrong; they will only see that words go unheeded and conclude that the offer was made but never meant.

sentences.zh: 愚以告下之事可小須後。

translations.literal: We foolishly think matters proclaimed to the people below might wait a little before being announced.
translations.idiomatic: We would respectfully suggest that this proclamation to the people be postponed a little.

sentences.zh: 」沈又教曰：「夫興益於上，受分於下，斯乃君子之操，何不言之有！

translations.literal: " Shen issued another instruction, saying: "When benefits are raised from above and shares received from below— this is the conduct of a gentleman. Why would there be any lack of people who speak!"
translations.idiomatic: Shen issued another instruction: "When superiors create benefits and subordinates receive their share, that is the way of a gentleman— why should anyone fail to speak up!"

sentences.zh: 」褚□復白曰：「堯、舜、周公所以能致忠諫者，以其款誠之心著也。

translations.literal: " Chu □ reported again, saying: "It is because Yao, Shun, and the Duke of Zhou could elicit loyal remonstrance that their sincere hearts were manifest."
translations.idiomatic: Chu Lüe reported again, "Yao, Shun, and the Duke of Zhou were able to draw forth loyal remonstrance because their own sincerity was plain for all to see."

sentences.zh: 冰炭不言而冷熱之質自明者，以其有實也。

translations.literal: Ice and charcoal need not speak for the nature of cold and heat to make itself clear— because they have substance.
translations.idiomatic: Ice and charcoal need not speak for their cold and heat to be known— because their nature is real.

sentences.zh: 若好忠直，如冰炭之自然，則諤諤之言將不求而自至。

translations.literal: If one loves loyalty and forthrightness as naturally as ice and charcoal differ, then blunt remonstrances will come without being sought.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly love loyalty and straight talk as naturally as ice differs from fire, blunt counsel will come without being sought.

sentences.zh: 若德不足以配唐、虞，明不足以並周公，實不可以同冰炭，是懸重賞，忠諫之言未可致也。

translations.literal: If one's virtue is not sufficient to match Tang and Yu, one's clarity not sufficient to equal the Duke of Zhou, and one's substance truly cannot compare with ice and charcoal— then to hang out heavy rewards, loyal remonstrances cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: If your virtue does not match that of Tang and Yu, your wisdom does not equal the Duke of Zhou's, and your substance is not as real as ice and charcoal, then hanging out heavy rewards will not bring loyal remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 」沈乃止。

translations.literal: " Shen then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shen then dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公下景元二年（

translations.literal: Under the Duke of Gaoguixiang, second year of Jingyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Under the Duke of Gaoguixiang, second year of Jingyuan (

sentences.zh: 辛巳，公元二六一年）

translations.literal: xinsi, AD 261)
translations.idiomatic: the year xinsi, AD 261)

sentences.zh: 春，三月，襄陽太守胡烈表言：「吳將鄧由、李光等十八屯同謀歸化，遣使送質任，欲令郡兵臨江迎拔。

translations.literal: Spring, third month: Administrator of Xiangyang Hu Lie submitted a memorial, saying: "Wu generals Deng You, Li Guang, and eighteen garrison posts together plotted to submit and be transformed; they sent envoys with hostages and wished the commandery troops to come to the river to welcome and extricate them."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of spring, Administrator of Xiangyang Hu Lie memorialized the throne: "Wu generals Deng You and Li Guang, together with eighteen garrison posts, have conspired to defect. They have sent envoys with hostages and ask that our commandery troops cross the river to receive them."

sentences.zh: 」詔王基部分諸軍徑造沮水以迎之。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered Wang Ji to divide the various armies and proceed directly to the Ju River to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Wang Ji to deploy the armies and march straight to the Ju River to receive them.

sentences.zh: 「若由等如期到者，便當因此震盪江表。

translations.literal: "If You and the others arrive on schedule, we should then by this means shake the lands south of the Yangzi."
translations.idiomatic: "If You and the others arrive on schedule, we should use the opportunity to shake the south of the Yangzi."

sentences.zh: 」基馳驛遺司馬昭書，說由等可疑之狀，「且當清澄，未宜便舉重兵深入應之。

translations.literal: " Ji sent a fast courier with a letter to Sima Zhao, describing the suspicious circumstances of You and the others: "For now we should clarify matters; it is not yet fitting to raise a heavy army and advance deep to respond."
translations.idiomatic: Ji sent an urgent dispatch to Sima Zhao describing the suspicious circumstances surrounding You and the others: "We should first verify the facts. It is not yet wise to commit a large force and advance deep into enemy country in response."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「夷陵東西道皆險狹，竹木叢蔚，卒有要害，弩馬不陳。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The eastern and western routes through Yiling are all narrow and perilous, with dense bamboo and trees. If there is suddenly a choke point, crossbows and cavalry cannot be deployed."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "The eastern and western routes through Yiling are narrow and treacherous, choked with bamboo and forest. At a sudden choke point, neither archers nor cavalry can be brought into formation."

sentences.zh: 今者筋角濡弱，水潦方降，廢盛農之務，徼難必之利，此事之危者也。

translations.literal: At present bow sinews and horn are damp and weak, floods are just descending, the great work of agriculture is abandoned, and difficult-to-obtain profits are sought— this affair is dangerous.
translations.idiomatic: Right now bowstrings and horn are sodden and weak, the rains are just beginning, peak farming season is being abandoned, and we would gamble on uncertain gains— this is a dangerous course.

sentences.zh: 姜維之趣上圭阜，文欽之據壽春，皆深入求利，以取覆沒，此近事之鑒戒也。
