translations.literal: Jiang Wei's rush to Shanggui Mound and Wen Qin's seizure of Shouchun both advanced deep seeking profit and ended in total destruction— these are recent warnings.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei's thrust toward Shanggui and Wen Qin's occupation of Shouchun both pushed deep for gain and ended in ruin— recent lessons close at hand.

sentences.zh: 嘉平已來，累有內難，當今之宜，當務鎮安社稷，撫寧上下，力農務本，懷柔百姓，未宜動眾以求外利也。

translations.literal: Since the Jiaping era there have repeatedly been internal crises. The proper course at present is to secure and settle the altars of soil and grain, pacify superiors and inferiors, exert strength in agriculture and attend to fundamentals, and soothe the common people— it is not yet fitting to move the masses seeking external profit.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jiaping era we have suffered repeated internal crises. The urgent task now is to stabilize the state, reassure court and country, devote ourselves to agriculture, and care for the people— not to mobilize armies in pursuit of external gain.

sentences.zh: 」昭累得基書，意狐疑，敕諸軍已上道者，且權停住所在，須候節度。

translations.literal: " Zhao repeatedly received Ji's letters and grew doubtful in mind. He ordered the armies already on the road to halt temporarily where they were and await further command.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao received letter after letter from Ji and grew uncertain. He ordered the armies already on the march to halt where they were for the time being and await further orders.

sentences.zh: 基復遺昭書曰：「昔漢祖納酈生之說，欲封六國，寤張良之謀而趣銷印。

translations.literal: Ji again sent Zhao a letter, saying: "In antiquity Emperor Gao of Han accepted Li Yiji's proposal and wished to enfeoff the Six States; he awoke to Zhang Liang's counsel and hastened to melt the seals."
translations.idiomatic: Ji wrote again to Zhao: "Long ago Emperor Gao of Han accepted Li Yiji's advice and was ready to enfeoff the Six States; then he heeded Zhang Liang and hurried to destroy the seals."

sentences.zh: 基謀慮淺短，誠不及留侯，亦懼襄陽有食其之謬。

translations.literal: Ji's planning and thought are shallow and short; truly he does not reach the Marquis of Liu, yet he also fears that Xiangyang may have a blunder like that of Yiji.
translations.idiomatic: My counsel is shallow and I am no match for the Marquis of Liu, but I fear Xiangyang may be repeating Yiji's mistake.

sentences.zh: 」昭於是罷兵，報基書曰：「凡處事者多曲相從順，鮮能確然共盡理實，誠感忠愛，每見規示，輒依來旨，已罷軍嚴。

translations.literal: " Zhao thereupon dismissed the armies and replied to Ji in a letter: "In handling affairs most people bend to agree and follow along; few can together firmly exhaust reason and fact. I am truly moved by loyal affection; whenever I see your admonitions I follow your intent. The armies have already been dismissed and martial readiness ended."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao then stood the armies down and wrote back to Ji: "In affairs of state most men simply agree with whatever is proposed; few speak plainly to the truth. I am deeply moved by your loyalty. Whenever you counsel me I follow your meaning. The troops have already been stood down."

sentences.zh: 」既而由等果不降。

translations.literal: " Soon afterward You and the others indeed did not defect.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, You and the others did not defect after all.

sentences.zh: 烈，奮之弟也。

translations.literal: Lie was Fen's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Lie was the younger brother of Hu Fen.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，甲寅，覆命司馬昭進爵位如前，不受。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, day jiayin: the command was renewed for Sima Zhao to advance in rank and enfeoffment as before; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn, on the jiayin day, Sima Zhao was again offered advancement in rank and enfeoffment as before; he declined.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，漢主以董厥為輔國大將軍，諸葛瞻為都護、衛將軍，共平尚書事，以侍中樊建為尚書令。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: the Han ruler appointed Dong Jue as General Who Supports the State, Zhuge Zhan as Director-General and Defender-in-Chief to jointly oversee Masters of Writing affairs, and Attendant-in-Ordinary Fan Jian as Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, the Han ruler appointed Dong Jue General Who Supports the State, made Zhuge Zhan Director-General and Defender-in-Chief to share oversight of the Masters of Writing, and appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary Fan Jian Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時中常侍黃皓用事，厥、瞻皆不能矯正，士大夫多附之，唯建不與皓往來。

translations.literal: At the time the Regular Palace Attendant Huang Hao wielded power. Neither Jue nor Zhan could correct this. Many gentry and officials attached themselves to him; only Jian did not associate with Hao.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the eunuch Huang Hao held power. Neither Dong Jue nor Zhuge Zhan could check him. Many officials attached themselves to Hao; only Fan Jian refused to have dealings with him.

sentences.zh: 秘書令郤正久在內職，與皓比屋，周旋三十餘年，澹然自守，以書自娛，既不為皓所愛，亦不為皓所憎，故官不過六百石，而亦不罹其禍。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Xi Zheng had long served in inner posts; he lived next door to Hao and moved in the same circles for more than thirty years. He kept himself detached and amused himself with books. Hao neither favored nor hated him, so his rank never exceeded six-hundred-bushel level, yet he also did not suffer disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Xi Zheng had long served in the inner offices, lived next door to Hao, and moved in the same circles for more than thirty years. He kept himself aloof and amused himself with books. Hao neither favored nor hated him, so his rank never rose above six-hundred-bushel level— yet he also escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 漢主弟甘陵王永憎皓，皓譖之，使十年不得朝見。

translations.literal: The Han ruler's younger brother, Prince Yong of Ganling, hated Hao. Hao slandered him, so that for ten years he could not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler's younger brother, Prince Yong of Ganling, despised Hao. Hao slandered him, and for ten years the prince was barred from attending court.

sentences.zh: 吳主使五官中郎將薛珝聘於漢，及還，吳主問漢政得失，對曰：「主暗而不知其過，臣下容身以求免罪，入其朝不聞直言，經其野民皆菜色。

translations.literal: The ruler of Wu sent Palace Gentleman Xue Xu on a mission of courtesy to Han. When he returned, the ruler of Wu asked about the strengths and faults of Han governance. He replied: "The ruler is dark and does not know his faults; his ministers preserve themselves seeking to escape punishment. Entering his court one does not hear straight speech; passing through his countryside the people all have the color of famine."
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Wu sent Palace Gentleman Xue Xu on a diplomatic mission to Han. On his return, the Wu ruler asked about the state of Han governance. Xu replied, "The ruler is benighted and does not know his own faults; his ministers merely save themselves to avoid punishment. In his court one hears no plain speaking; in his countryside the people wear the look of famine."

sentences.zh: 臣聞燕雀處堂，子母相樂，自以為至安也，突決棟焚，而燕雀怡然不知禍之將及，其是之謂乎！

translations.literal: I have heard that when swallows and sparrows dwell in the hall, mother and young rejoice together and deem themselves utterly secure— then suddenly the ridge beam bursts and the house burns, yet the swallows and sparrows remain at ease, unaware that disaster is about to overtake them. Is this not the very thing!
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when swallows and sparrows nest in the rafters, mother and young take their ease and think themselves perfectly secure— then the beam splits and the house catches fire, yet the birds remain content, unaware that ruin is near. Is this not exactly what we see?

sentences.zh: 」珝，綜之子也。

translations.literal: " Xu was Zong's son.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xu was the son of Xue Zong.

sentences.zh: 是歲，鮮卑索頭部大人拓跋力微，始遣其子沙漠汗入貢，因留為質。

translations.literal: That year, Tuoba Liwei, chieftain of the Suotou branch of the Xianbei, for the first time sent his son Shamo Han to pay tribute and had him remain as a hostage.
translations.idiomatic: That year Tuoba Liwei, chieftain of the Suotou Xianbei, sent his son Shamo Han to pay tribute for the first time and left him behind as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 力微之先世居北荒，不交南夏。

translations.literal: Liwei's forebears dwelt in the northern wilds and had no dealings with the southern Xia lands.
translations.idiomatic: Liwei's ancestors had lived in the northern wastes and had no contact with the Chinese south.

sentences.zh: 至可汗毛，始強大，統國三十六，大姓九十九。

translations.literal: Down to Khan Mao, they first grew powerful, ruling thirty-six states and ninety-nine great clans.
translations.idiomatic: Under Khan Mao they first grew powerful, ruling thirty-six states and ninety-nine great clans.

sentences.zh: 後五世至可汗推寅，南遷大澤。

translations.literal: Five generations later came Khan Tuiyin, who migrated south to the Great Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations later, under Khan Tuiyin, they migrated south to the Great Marsh.

sentences.zh: 又七世至可汗鄰，使其兄弟七人及族人乙旃氏、車惃氏分統部眾為十族。

translations.literal: Seven generations later came Khan Lin, who had his seven brothers and clansmen of the Yizhan and Chehun clans divide rule over the tribes into ten groups.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations after that, under Khan Lin, he had his seven brothers and the clans Yizhan and Chehun divide the tribes into ten groups.

sentences.zh: 鄰老，以位授其子詰汾，使南遷，遂居匈奴故地。

translations.literal: When Lin grew old, he passed the position to his son Jiefen, sent him to migrate south, and thus they settled in the former lands of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin grew old, he passed leadership to his son Jiefen and sent him south; they settled in the former Xiongnu territory.

sentences.zh: 詰汾卒，力微立，復徙居定襄之盛樂，部眾浸盛，諸部皆畏服之。

translations.literal: When Jiefen died, Liwei succeeded. They moved again to Shengle in Dingxiang; the tribes gradually flourished, and all the branches feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiefen died, Liwei succeeded him. They moved again to Shengle in Dingxiang; their following steadily grew, and all the tribes came to fear and obey him.
